title: Condition-transfer estimand E-CT: same-lab, same-extractant mean-sibling template with sibling-count shrinkage, a 0-4 read ladder, a harm rule and publication-unit inference
lens: regime / estimand reframing (known laboratory and extractant, new condition) + evaluation unit design
hypothesis: When a laboratory already has at least 2 full series of the same extractant at other conditions, the mean-sibling template plus PWL_R of the read residuals, shrunk toward B1 by w = n/(n+K), predicts strict-adjacent log SF at the new condition clearly better than B1 at 4 reads (>= +0.05 R2 without C5-BTBP and near-copies). With only one prior series there is no gain. The gain is consistent across publications but not yet across source clusters.
rationale: The systematic remainder after B1 is source-local (roughness r +0.36 within publication x extractant, about 0 across publications), so BP/BPG removes it by construction. H-SIBLING is ranked first in the evidence base, but gap G2 is open: no combination rule, no sibling-count dependence, no k ladder, no unit of inference. The knowledge state matches a real question (I ran this extractant before; how few metals at the new acidity?). It must be registered as its own estimand.
evidence_for:
Exploratory, BPG, 5 seeds, E6 rows (1,111 rows/seed, 149 cells, 19 publications), E6 reproduced exactly.
- Mean template 0.573, shrunk (K=2) 0.594 vs B1 0.449.
- Read ladder 0/2/3/4 reads: 0.411 / 0.517 / 0.554 / 0.573 vs D7 - / 0.193 / 0.403 / 0.447.
- n_sib >= 2, no C5-BTBP (112 cells): 0.675 / 0.682 vs B1 0.510; 2 reads 0.595.
- Leave-one-publication-out gain +0.125 (se 0.044, min +0.100); 14/19 publications improve; publication sign test p 0.032, IM-t p 0.001.
- Laboratory-specific: other-publication same-extractant template 0.401 vs 0.386; other-extractant same-publication template 0.336 vs 0.476.
- Mean of all siblings beats nearest-condition sibling (0.573 vs 0.537).
evidence_against:
- Gain is an averaging effect: a single random sibling scores 0.290 (worse than B1); n_sib = 1 stratum 0.513 vs B1 0.544.
- Three publications carry about 86 % of the gain (C5-BTBP about 42 %, whose siblings share a suspected floor); positive-gain Kish 4.5.
- By cluster only 4 wins / 3 losses (sign-flip p 0.18); three small single-publication clusters with 1-2 siblings lose 26-37 % SSE.
- Outside the giant cluster without C5-BTBP raw SIB loses (0.440 vs 0.470); only the shrunk version wins (0.536).
- Near-copies (shape sd < 0.02; 47/149 cells) inflate win counts. K = 2 and the stratum cut were chosen after seeing rows; the two source analyses disagree on the cut (>= 2 vs >= 3 siblings).
test_design:
1. Register E-CT separately; never compared with or substituted for the BP/BPG 0.452.
2. Population: C3 cells with >= 1 same-publication, same-extractant cell covering the target metals (metadata only). Hold out one condition at a time.
3. Pre-declared strata: n_sib = 1, 2, >= 3 (2-7 and >= 8 as sensitivity).
4. Reads: DOPT_Q nested sets at 0, 2, 3, 4 reads on rows identical to REF.
5. Frozen predictor: T = mean sibling curve; SIB = T + PWL_R(y_S - T_S) along -r(CN8); SH = w*SIB + (1-w)*B1 with w = n/(n+2); variant K chosen leave-one-publication-out.
6. Baselines on identical rows: B1 at same k and at 4 reads, copy-mean (0 reads), nearest-condition sibling, random single sibling (exact expectation), publication x pair offsets (nested K).
7. Controls: same-extractant other-publication template; other-extractant same-publication template; near-copy and SF-twin exclusion; without C5-BTBP; inside |predicted level| <= 2.
8. Inference: unit = publication x extractant; IM-t with the size correction from M36 (or a chemotype-stratified permutation), cluster sign-flip as reported sensitivity; per-publication relative SSE and top-3 share.
9. Harm rule: in the 1-2-sibling stratum SH may not be worse than B1 by > 5 % relative SSE, else the deployed rule depends on sibling count.
10. Secondary: lab-conditional conformal 80 % intervals. Confirmation on new multi-condition publications after freezing (M05).
kill_criterion: Claim abandoned if any holds: (a) n_sib >= 2, no C5-BTBP, no near-copies: SH(4 reads) - B1(4 reads) < +0.05 R2 or publication-jackknife 95 % lower bound <= 0; (b) SH with 2 reads < 0.50 in that stratum; (c) the other-publication template reaches >= 70 % of the gain on overlapping rows; (e) on >= 5 new publications SH - B1 < +0.03. If only the equal-weight gain outside the giant cluster is <= 0, narrow the claim to DGA-type labs with dense condition grids. No gain at n_sib = 1 restricts the claim ('needs >= 2 prior series'); it does not kill it.
expected_effect: n_sib >= 2 without C5-BTBP: about 0.65-0.68 at 4 reads vs B1 about 0.51; about 0.57-0.60 at 2 reads (above B1 with 4 reads and no history). n_sib = 1: about 0. Equal-cluster gain much smaller than pooled (about +7 % vs +23 % SSE). On new data expect +0.05 to +0.10.
practical_value: A budget rule for a chemist: with >= 2 prior own series of the extractant, measure 2 metals at the new condition and use the mean of the old series as template; with one prior series use B1 with 4 metals; curves of the same extractant from other laboratories are not a substitute. Turns a condition scan into full series at 2-3 anchor conditions plus 2 metals elsewhere.
risks: Same-paper shared artefacts (floor, calibration, re-reports) make the template predict errors; few publications drive the gain; K and strata are post hoc; strong publication dependence; must never be quoted beside 0.452; confirmation needs new multi-condition series the archive lacks.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-1, evaluation-5; adds to H-SIBLING / E6 6.8 the 0-4 read ladder, the finding that the gain needs >= 2 siblings (averaging), a sibling-count shrinkage rule that rescues non-giant clusters, a harm rule, and the publication-vs-cluster unit split (14/5 vs 4/3).

title: Low-read operating point inside condition transfer: 2 reads plus a sibling vs B1 at 4 reads, with an additive shift-plus-tilt deformation model and a proportional-scaling control
lens: measurement design (k ladder, cost model) + physics of condition change (slope analysis)
hypothesis: For the same extractant in the same laboratory, a condition change mainly shifts every Ln equally and adds a smooth tilt, while metal-specific anomalies stay fixed. So 2 well-placed reads at the new condition plus a sibling template predict adjacent log SF at least as well as B1 with 4 reads and no sibling, and additive deformation beats proportional (LFER) rescaling of the template.
rationale: In the condition-transfer regime the expensive unit is the condition, and gap G2 lists k = 0-2 behaviour as unreported. Slope analysis gives a pre-declarable family of deformations ordered by the reads they need (copy, shift, shift+tilt, full PWL), which turns the low-read ladder into a falsifiable physical claim rather than a tuning exercise.
evidence_for:
Exploratory, E6 rows, DOPT_Q reads.
- SIB with 2 DOPT_Q-nested reads 0.517 vs D7 with 4 reads 0.447; near-copies excluded 0.490 vs 0.423.
- Near-copies excluded: dominant cluster 0.602 vs 0.500 (75 cells); other clusters 0.408 vs 0.366 (27 cells).
- Shift only (1 read) = copy 0.411: a pure shift cancels in log SF, as predicted.
- 2 extreme reads 0.492; 2 middle reads 0.441 (tilt needs a lever arm).
- Additive 4-read template 0.573 vs LFER-scaled 0.525.
- Gd chord does not move with acid within an extractant (rho 0.07, n 61).
evidence_against:
- 2-read placement is unsettled: extremes-first is worse than DOPT_Q-nested 2 reads (0.489-0.492 vs 0.517), and the 2-read subsets were taken from DOPT_Q 4-read sets, not designed.
- Going from 2 to 4 reads adds about +0.08, so the change is more than shift + tilt.
- At shape sd >= 0.05 the 2-read advantage vanishes (+0.009); only 27 cells lie outside the dominant cluster.
- Single-sibling templates are poor (M01); template rules were chosen on these cells.
test_design: Inside E-CT (M01), condition hold-out within publication x extractant, pre-declared near-copy exclusion (shape sd < 0.02). Deformation ladder on identical rows: D0 copy; D1 shift (1 read, lightest measured metal); D2 shift+tilt with the lightest and heaviest measured metals (label-free); D2-DOPT (DOPT_Q-nested 2 reads); D2-LS (least-squares shift+tilt on the 4 reads, no PWL); D4 additive PWL; negative control D4-scaled (proportional LFER). Baselines B1 at 4 reads and B1 at 2 reads (same metals). Primary contrast SIB at 2 reads - B1 at 4 reads, cluster_cpg intervals, split dominant cluster vs rest and by condition-distance tertile; balanced MAE.
kill_criterion: Killed if: SIB(2 reads) - B1(4 reads) <= 0 in the near-copy-excluded, non-dominant-cluster stratum; or the overall cluster lower bound < -0.02; or D2 fails to beat B1(4 reads) by >= +0.02 in >= 4/5 seeds after near-copy exclusion; or the gain disappears when the template is the single nearest condition instead of the mean; or D4-scaled >= D4 (refutes the additive model).
expected_effect: SIB(2 reads) - B1(4 reads) about +0.04 to +0.10; D2 about 0.47-0.49 vs B1 about 0.43-0.45 after near-copy exclusion; D4 near 0.55-0.57.
practical_value: After one or more full series of an extractant, each new acidity, concentration or diluent needs only 2 metals (which 2 is decided by the test) to match a 4-metal measurement without a reference. Shift and tilt the old series; do not rescale it. Halves the assay load wherever each metal costs a separate determination, and lets literature miners complete partial series within a paper.
risks: Near-copies and shared stocks inflate every sibling number; curves that turn over at the heavy end may break shift+tilt; separate estimand only; post hoc template rules.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-3, physics-3; fills the k < 3 part of G2, refutes proportional deformation (0.525 vs 0.573), and records the open conflict on 2-read placement (extremes 0.489-0.492 vs DOPT_Q-nested 0.517) as a pre-declared crossing.

title: Sibling weighting rule head-to-head: condition-kernel empirical-Bayes BLUP vs read-level matching vs the plain mean template
lens: statistical modelling of laboratory random effects (EB shrinkage, condition kernel) vs label-free level matching
hypothesis: How siblings are weighted matters. Either (a) an empirical-Bayes BLUP of B1 residuals from siblings, weighted by an acid-distance kernel and shrunk by sibling count (two levels: same extractant; other extractant of the same publication), or (b) averaging the two siblings whose levels at the 4 reads are closest (label-free), beats the unweighted mean template and B1 on identical rows. A level-farthest or random single sibling is worse than B1, and per-metal extrapolation of acid trends fails.
rationale: Gap G2 asks how to combine several siblings and how condition distance matters. The two candidate answers point to different distance axes (acid distance vs read-level distance), so they are competitors and should be scored head-to-head inside one registration rather than as separate claims.
evidence_for:
(a) Kernel BLUP (nested hyperparameters, leave-publication-out scalars): all C3 rows 0.564 vs B1 0.452; rows with a same-extractant sibling 0.626 vs unshrunk template 0.567; without C5-BTBP 0.571; outside the big cluster 0.567; near-identical siblings dropped 0.546. Single-sibling residual correlation decays with |dlog acid| (0.60 up to 0.2; 0.14 at 0.5-1; 0.04 above 1). Shrinkage slope 0.30 for one sibling vs 0.74-0.91 for >= 2. Read ladder 0/2/3/4: 0.312 / 0.465 / 0.535 / 0.567.
(b) 127 cells with >= 2 siblings: mean of 2 level-nearest 0.620, mean all 0.577, level-nearest 0.537, condition-nearest 0.511, random single 0.225, level-farthest -0.864, B1 0.415 (without C5-BTBP 0.695 / 0.675 / 0.646 / 0.569 / - / - / 0.510). Acid-trend extrapolation -0.064. Diluent-only siblings copy MSE 0.0086 vs acid-only 0.049.
evidence_against:
- Both rule families were designed after seeing these rows.
- Kernel BLUP loses 12.5 % SSE in one cluster and 6-20 % in 4 chemotypes.
- With exactly 3 siblings mean-all beats mean-of-2 (0.775 vs 0.761); level-nearest vs condition-nearest differ by only 0.026, and level and condition distance are confounded.
- About 19 families, dominated by the giant DGA cluster; median-of-siblings gives no robustness gain.
test_design: Inside E-CT (M01), identical rows and reads (ladder at 2, 3, 4 reads). Arms: B1; mean-all template; nearest-condition (pre-declared distance |dlog acid| + |dlog L| + diluent flag); nearest-level; mean of 2 nearest-level; kernel EB BLUP with nested grid ell {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, inf}, rho {0, 0.3, 0.6}, kappa {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}, inner leave-publication-block-out, one-SE rule toward the mean template; publication x pair offsets. Controls: random single (expectation), level-farthest (must be worst), acid values shuffled within publication (tests the kernel), other-publication siblings (negative). Pre-declared near-copy exclusion. Family-cluster bootstrap and leave-one-family-out; report without giant cluster and C5-BTBP; sibling-count x reads subsampling surface. Confirmatory rows only from new families (M05).
kill_criterion: Kernel: nested all-row R2 < 0.52 at 4 reads, or gain over the refitted mean template < +0.01 on covered rows, or the acid-shuffle control within 0.005 (drop the kernel, keep plain EB). Level rule: mean-of-2-level-nearest minus mean-all <= 0 (90 % interval includes -0.01) and level-nearest <= condition-nearest, or level-farthest not the worst arm. If both die, register mean-all only.
expected_effect: +0.01 to +0.06 over the mean template on covered rows; one distance axis likely dominates. All-row R2 about 0.54-0.57 at 4 reads in this regime.
practical_value: Tells a chemist which old series to reuse: matched D level and nearby acidity; average at least two; never extrapolate acid trends metal by metal; diluent swaps preserve adjacent SF better than acid changes.
risks: Post hoc rules; few families; same-paper artefacts; a separate estimand that must not be compared with BP/BPG numbers.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: statistics-1, contrarian-2; merges two competing answers to G2 into one crossing, with the sibling-count shrinkage law and the finding that a random single sibling is worse than B1.

title: Choose conditions, not metals: active selection of which conditions get full series
lens: active learning over the real cost unit (the experiment)
hypothesis: A lab characterising one extractant across C conditions first screens every condition with 4 reads, then measures full series at conditions spread over the screen-level quantiles (SPREAD) and predicts the rest from them. This predicts the remaining conditions better than random, central or extreme choices and reaches R2 >= 0.50 with 2 full series.
rationale: With ICP-MS the cost unit is the experiment, and metal-placement policies are exhausted at k = 3 (+0.006). Nobody has optimised which conditions to characterise fully. Template quality depends on level matching (M03), so library coverage of the level range is the natural objective.
evidence_for: 11 families with >= 5 C3 cells, non-library rows. n = 2: SPREAD 0.541, CENTRAL 0.497, RANDOM 0.401, EXTREME -0.03, B1 0.425. n = 3: 0.557 / 0.440 / 0.462 / 0.075 / 0.40. Without C5-BTBP at n = 2: SPREAD 0.583 vs RANDOM 0.529 (B1 0.531). Sibling dose-response MSE 0.0298 / 0.0222 / 0.0198 / 0.0185 for 1-4 random references vs B1 0.0214.
evidence_against: Only 11 families, one cluster dominant; the predictor rule came from the same data; literature condition sets were not designed; with ICP-MS a 4-read screen costs as much as a full series, so the screen is cheap only for subset feeds or partially reported literature conditions.
test_design: Registered simulation on all C3 families with >= 4 cells, BPG DOPT_Q reads, 5 seeds, budgets n = 1-3 full series. Policies: RANDOM (exact expectation over subsets), SPREAD (quantiles of screen level = mean of the 4 reads), CENTRAL, EXTREME, MAXMIN-LEVEL. Predictor frozen from the M03 winner (mean-all if M03 dies). Comparators B1 and copy-mean on identical rows. Family-cluster bootstrap and leave-one-family-out. Primary SPREAD - RANDOM at n = 2; secondary the first n with non-library R2 >= 0.50.
kill_criterion: Killed if SPREAD - RANDOM at n = 2 < +0.03 or its 90 % family interval includes 0, or SPREAD < B1 at n = 2.
expected_effect: About +0.1 over random selection at n = 2; within-lab non-library R2 0.50-0.58 with 2 full series; extreme-first clearly harmful.
practical_value: Campaign protocol: scan candidate conditions cheaply, fully characterise 2-3 conditions spaced across the middle of the D range, never anchor references on extreme conditions (log D < -2 or > 2), cover the rest with 4-read checks.
risks: Tiny family count; depends on M03's predictor; may fail where conditions change stoichiometry; separate within-lab estimand.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: contrarian-3; first active-learning loop over conditions rather than metals.

title: External test of condition transfer on new non-DGA multi-condition publications
lens: new data acquisition (open-access literature with provenance), confirmation of a regime
hypothesis: The sibling-template gain generalises beyond DGA: on new non-DGA multi-condition publications the median per-publication relative pair-SSE reduction of the frozen template vs B1 is > 0 on in-window rows.
rationale: Stratified in-corpus checks suggest the gain is a DGA phenomenon plus out-of-window rows. Only new non-DGA multi-condition series, read after freezing, can settle this, and several verified open-access candidates are exactly such designs (acid, extractant concentration and diluent scans).
evidence_for: E6 reproduced (0.573 vs 0.449); 14/19 publications positive; roughness r +0.36 within publication x extractant. Verified open-access multi-condition non-DGA candidates exist (phenanthroline-diamide diluent and acid scans with numeric SI tables, a phosphonium nitrate system, organophosphorus acid in two diluents). Figure-sourced cells are not rougher than table cells, so plotted-only sources are admissible (M22).
evidence_against: In C3: sc009 0.700 vs 0.515; non-sc009 0.485 vs 0.400; non-sc009 in-window rows 0.569 vs B1 0.598 (no gain); only 4/7 non-sc009 publications positive and three N-donor/amide publications lose (-0.26 to -0.37). Power: 0.40-0.45 at 5 publications, 0.50-0.53 at 6, 0.76 at 10, 0.84 at 12 (weaker under the non-DGA distribution). Diluent changes are larger perturbations than acid changes. Automated search yield is low.
test_design: Register E-SIB before extraction: anchor = condition with most in-window metals; template rule frozen from M01/M03; near-copy exclusion; DOPT_Q at 4 reads with 2- and 3-read ladder. An analyst extracts each series (two independent digitisations for plots) and gives the scorer only the anchor series and the read metals of each target condition. Score all strict-adjacent pairs with SIB, B1 (frozen corpus beta) and copy-sibling. Primary: per-publication relative pair-SSE of SIB vs B1, in-window and all rows separately. Controls: B1, copy-sibling, other-extractant shuffled sibling. Add the user's own lab series where available. Check authors and ligands for overlap with corpus groups first; skip any figure without D on the axis.
kill_criterion: With >= 6 new non-DGA publications: median gain <= 0 on in-window rows, or <= 3/6 positive, declares the sibling gain DGA- or shared-artefact-specific and B1 is recommended for non-DGA users. >= 5/6 positive with median >= 0.15 promotes the regime, pending >= 10 publications.
expected_effect: Prior: about 0 for in-window non-DGA rows; likely mixed signs across publications.
practical_value: Answers a process chemist's question: with one full series of this ligand, after changing acid or diluent, can 4 metals be trusted for adjacent SFs, and for which donor classes.
risks: Candidate list chosen after the stratification (lead); digitisation and unit conversions; author overlap; one publication carries many rows (analyse at publication level); no downloads without the user's permission.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-3; the in-window non-DGA null (0.569 vs 0.598) and per-publication power numbers are new, as is targeting open-access multi-condition non-DGA designs.

title: Value-of-prior-information ladder (S0-S4), with the same-publication other-extractant channel split into homologue chemistry vs laboratory fingerprint
lens: regime / estimand reframing (knowledge states) + meta-analysis of laboratory effects with placebo channels
hypothesis: Information beyond B1 is laboratory-local and extractant-specific: other labs' curves of the same chemotype (S1) or extractant (S2) add < +0.02 without C5-BTBP; the lab's own data on other extractants (S3) add +0.01 to +0.05, and that part comes from same-chemotype homologues rather than a generic laboratory or analytical fingerprint; only the lab's own series of the same extractant (S4) add >= +0.10. S0 (nothing known) stays the primary estimand.
rationale: A chemist planning a 4-metal campaign must decide what prior information to collect. Round 4 posed only S0. If S3 were an instrument fingerprint, a lab could calibrate it once (a cheap product); if it is homologue chemistry, the deployable regime is a ligand-design lab's own homologue history. The two explanations of the same channel compete and are tested together.
evidence_for: S1: blend +0.015 without C5-BTBP. S2: +0.008 without C5-BTBP (the 50/50 blend looks like +0.051 with it). S3: publication x pair offsets K = 5 / 10 give 0.474 / 0.478 vs B1 0.455 (K = 0: 0.291); on cells without a same-extractant sibling 0.460 vs 0.412. Channel split: other extractant same publication 0.4624 vs other chemotype same publication 0.4534 vs B1 0.4521; random-publication placebo 0.414-0.441; homologue rows 0.4888 vs 0.4666. S4: 0.580-0.594. Roughness r +0.36 / +0.14 / -0.02. An oxide-interference model predicts roughness at r -0.05, no better than shifted-table placebos; the Gd dip is larger at small Pr:Gd ratio, opposite to the artefact prediction.
evidence_against: S3 gain small and K-sensitive (K chosen on these rows); concentrated in 2 clusters, one cluster loses; 10 publications improve, 6 worsen; S1/S2 rest on 2-7 chemotypes; homologue channel may include copy groups; E2's cross-publication same-extractant residual correlation 0.10-0.14 leaves a little room for S2; the calibration mechanism (per-metal level offsets) is untested.
test_design: Define S0-S4 from metadata only; score each on its own eligible C3 rows at k = 3 DOPT_Q vs B1 on the same rows. Frozen predictor family: template blend with weight chosen leave-one-cluster-out; group x pair offsets K in {5, 10} (20 as sensitivity); for S3, separate homologue (same chemotype) and other-chemotype channels, and lab x metal level offsets vs pair offsets (calibration test); a homologue template. Hold-out for S3: one extractant (all its conditions) within publications with >= 2 extractants. Controls: random-publication placebo, copy-group exclusion, without C5-BTBP, inside the window. Inference unit publication (S3, S4) or cluster (S1, S2). Contrasts S2-S1, homologue - other chemotype, level vs pair offsets, S4-S3. Output a 5-row value-of-information table, each row its own estimand. One pre-declared refit of the interference model where isotopes are recorded.
kill_criterion: Lab-local thesis killed if S1 or S2 reaches >= +0.03 without C5-BTBP with leave-one-cluster-out weights and a positive bootstrap lower bound. S3 killed if < +0.01 at both K or < 60 % of publications improve. Homologue claim killed if homologue - B1 < +0.01 (or lower bound <= 0), if its sign flips when either contributing cluster is left out, or if other-chemotype >= homologue. Calibration explanation dropped if level offsets do not match or beat pair offsets.
expected_effect: S1 +0.01 to +0.02; S2 about +0.01; S3 +0.01 to +0.04, mostly homologue; S4 +0.10 to +0.17; S0 unchanged at 0.452.
practical_value: Tells a chemist what to collect before a cheap 4-metal campaign: own prior series of the same extractant >> own homologue data > other labs' curves (about nothing). Tighter instrument interference control will not remove adjacent-SF scatter, so no 'lab calibration' product. Curators should keep laboratory identity and per-lab series.
risks: S3 may be a publication artefact; few chemotypes; K chosen on these rows; temptation to quote S4 as 'the' result.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-2, contrarian-5; splits the within-source regime into knowledge states with specificity contrasts, answers G2's other-extractant share, and falsifies the analytical-fingerprint explanation.

title: Known-extractant estimand: transfer only the f-shell anomalies (Gd, and Nd for DGAs) from other publications
lens: physics and chemistry (condition-invariant f-shell anomalies) + publication hold-out
hypothesis: For an extractant or chemotype documented in other publications, transferring only its Gd dip and (for DGAs) its Nd dip, shrunk toward B1, beats B1 and the full cross-publication template on held-out publications; adding Ce or all metals makes it worse, because only these anomalies are reproducible chemistry.
rationale: The Gd dip has ICC 0.69 by extractant and does not move with acid within an extractant; the sc009 Nd dip appears in every sc009 publication; whole-curve copies across publications fail. A 2-number transfer is a physics-constrained, low-variance alternative to 14-offset corrections that failed under publication hold-out.
evidence_for: sc009 Nd chord negative in every publication (-0.04 to -0.22) vs +0.004 elsewhere. sc009 Nd potential chosen leave-one-publication-out: +0.0063 (5/5 seeds); sc009 Pr/Nd 0.26 -> 0.53. Same extractant, other publication (786 rows/seed): B1 0.386; Gd only 0.409; Gd+Nd 0.427; Gd+Nd+Ce 0.421; full template 0.401. Within publication about 45 % of the sibling gain is carried by three metal anomalies.
evidence_against: +1.29 of the +1.45 SSE/seed gain is C5-BTBP borrowing from a cell that may be the same data under another attribution; TODGA alone 0.438 -> 0.450; under BPG the estimand cannot be posed (all sc009 in one cluster), so it is a BP publication-hold-out claim only; the Nd chord deepens with acid (rho -0.36); S01 donor-class dips were null; grid values chosen on these rows.
test_design: Separate estimand E-KX: held-out-publication cells under BP folds whose extractant (Gd) or chemotype (Nd) has training cells in other publications. Pre-declared exclusions: copy groups and the suspected C5-BTBP duplicate pair; report with and without C5-BTBP. B1-KX: u_Gd(extractant) and u_Nd(chemotype) = training-publication mean chord anomaly, shrunk n/(n+5) toward B1's beta and 0, entered as point potentials (reads stay exact); unseen extractants fall back to B1. Controls: B1; full cross-publication template; anomalies from a random other extractant of the same family (200 draws); +Ce variant; all-12-metal variant. Endpoints: pooled R2, Pr/Nd and Gd-pair R2, per-publication contrasts, balanced MAE.
kill_criterion: On E-KX rows without C5-BTBP: gain < +0.005, or < 4/5 seeds positive, or the random-extractant permutation reaches the observed gain, or the +Ce or all-metal variant does as well or better.
expected_effect: +0.005 to +0.01 without C5-BTBP; sc009 Pr/Nd from about 0.26 to about 0.5.
practical_value: A chemist using a literature extractant under new conditions can borrow two numbers (its Gd dip and, for DGAs, its Nd dip) and improve Pr/Nd and Gd-region SF estimates; a Pr/Nd SF from plain DGA radius interpolation is too optimistic (matters for magnet-metal separation); do not borrow Ce or other roughness from other labs.
risks: Outside BPG by construction (must be labelled a separate deployment claim); few effective units; copy lineage inside the giant cluster.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: physics-2; first anomaly-only transfer by extractant under publication hold-out, and the decomposition showing Ce does not transfer while Gd and Nd do.

title: Variance budget of B1's residual (transferable / laboratory-shared / target-specific) with a sibling dose-response ceiling and a registered futility rule for 0.50 under BPG
lens: crossed random effects, noise-ceiling bounds, stop rule
hypothesis: B1's residual splits into a transferable part (chemotype or extractant x pair, declared condition slopes), a laboratory-shared part (publication, extractant x publication, condition kernel) and a target-specific part. The transferable part is below the 8.8 % of SSE needed to reach 0.50, and the target-specific part is >= 50 % of B1's MSE, so 0.50 at k = 3 under BPG is out of reach for cross-source models in the declared feature classes.
rationale: Routes have been closed one by one with weak power caveats. A joint budget answers once how much residual is reachable in principle for a new laboratory, how much needs a lab reference series, and how much is noise or idiosyncratic. A sibling-count dose-response gives an independent, model-free estimate of the unreachable part without a lab campaign.
evidence_for: Sibling dose-response (103 cells with >= 4 siblings): MSE(n) = a + b/n with a 0.0174, b 0.0179; a/B1 MSE 0.67 (0.59 without C5-BTBP); cap 0.584 vs B1 0.378 on those rows. Relation-class residual correlations: other extractant same publication 0.16 (similar for same and different chemotype, i.e. lab-like); same extractant same publication 0.36 (0.51 at near-identical conditions); same extractant other publication 0.10-0.14. Chemotype x pair offsets from other publications <= +0.006; cross-publication and analog templates do not beat B1 (0.404 vs 0.499; blend 0.4512 vs 0.4521). Near-condition bound: non-shared share of pair error <= 0.49 (mean-square) / 0.24 (rank). a/B1 close to the 15-cell replicate share 0.54.
evidence_against: Family-rich cells are about 45 % of rows and DGA-heavy; a includes condition-specific chemistry a condition-aware model might reach (copy error rises with |dlog acid|, rho +0.30); the 1/n fit has 4 points and heavy tails (dropping C5-BTBP halves a); with about 4 effective chemotypes the transferable interval may be too wide; futility is conditional on declared feature classes; Ce's acid slope is ambiguous (M28).
test_design: (1) Crossed random-effects (or relation-class moment) model of B1 hidden-level deviations, scored only through pair contrasts, metal-specific variances, Student-t errors; cluster_cpg bootstrap (2,000) and publication bootstrap; map to T, L, I shares. (2) Dose-response a + b/n on all cells with >= 2 siblings (subsets up to n = 6, <= 50 per n), per pair type, families weighted equally, family bootstrap; condition-aware within-family ridge arm (per-metal log D on log acid and log L, shrunk to family mean) to test whether a is reducible; placebo with random other-family siblings. (3) Validation: the budget must reproduce publication offsets 0.476-0.533, chemotype-from-other-publications about +0.006, kernel BLUP 0.564 (M03) and the 15-cell replicate share. Freeze the futility rule before fitting; report with and without C5-BTBP and the giant cluster.
kill_criterion: Decision rule: upper 95 % bound of T < 8.8 % of SSE registers futility for model-only routes to 0.50 under BPG (budget moves to known-lab regimes, more reads, measurement and provenance); lower bound >= 4.4 % justifies one powered model slot; otherwise inconclusive. Headroom remains (idea killed) if a/B1 MSE < 0.40 with interval excluding 0.5, or the condition-aware arm lowers a by >= 30 %, or extrapolated cross-source headroom > +0.05 with lower bound > +0.01. Budget invalid if it fails >= 2 of the 4 validation cross-fits.
expected_effect: T about 1-4 % (upper 5-9 %); L about 15-30 %; I about 45-60 %; cross-source headroom above B1 about +0.02 to +0.06.
practical_value: Decides whether to stop asking cross-source or structure models for adjacent SF from 4 metals and invest in reference series, extra reads or data quality. Without own-lab data, pair-level error below about 0.13 log should not be expected. Gives a software prior for the repeatability campaign (M11).
risks: Crossed models unstable on heavy-tailed unbalanced data (moment fallback); futility must be phrased as conditional on a seen corpus; lab identity approximated by publication; a only bounds noise from above.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: statistics-5, contrarian-1; first joint budget with an interval for the transferable share, a sibling-count dose-response ceiling, and a pre-registered futility rule.

title: Registered measurability domain: B1-predicted log D of both metals in [-2, 2], with a nested threshold, composition-matched abstention controls, mechanism checks and window-aware intervals
lens: label-free applicability domain / selective prediction, with a physical a priori threshold
hypothesis: Keeping pairs whose B1-predicted log D of both metals lies in [-2, 2] (declared a priori: one phase holds < 1 % outside it) gives R2 >= 0.50 on >= 70 % of rows, beats random abstention stratified by publication at matched coverage (so it flags rows, not only laboratories), survives leave-one-cluster-out, and leaves an out-of-window error that is unstructured tail noise with no correctable signature.
rationale: The window (0.540 on 74.7 %) beats unstratified random abstention, but the threshold was chosen post hoc, and C5-BTBP is 29 % of out-of-window rows, so part of the gain may be 'drop floor-limited labs'. Composition-matched controls separate the two mechanisms, and fixed mechanism checks decide whether any modelling slot should go to the out-of-window tail.
evidence_for: Threshold curve c = 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 / 3: coverage 0.455 / 0.603 / 0.747 / 0.847 / 0.927, inside R2 0.571 / 0.557 / 0.540 / 0.501 / 0.495. Nested threshold: 0.544 at 0.672 (coverage >= 0.6) and 0.527 at 0.753 (coverage >= 0.7). LOCO inside 0.505-0.551. MSE inside 0.0189 vs outside about 0.051. Random abstention: unstratified 0.453 [0.436, 0.468]; by pair type 0.4525; by cluster 0.472; by pair type x cluster 0.477; by publication 0.489 [0.473, 0.504], so about +0.036 composition and +0.051 within-publication selection. Within-pair-type R2 0.384 -> 0.480. Robust sd of chord deviations flat across level bins except below -3; no even/odd contamination signature outside C5-BTBP; a minority-phase-concentration window is worse (0.476); lab-shared roughness exists in window only (0.157 vs -0.029).
evidence_against: c = 2 was one of 4 windows tried; per-cluster coverage 0.19 in the BTBP cluster, so part is source exclusion; var(y) inside is lower (0.041 vs 0.049), so report MSE; a cross-fitted heteroscedastic variance model does worse (0.470 at 75 %), a warning that the window may be lucky; out-of-window rows are unbiased (slope 1.013), so there is no point-prediction fix; cleaner new data may shrink the contrast; small publications leave stratified controls little freedom.
test_design: Register E-AD. Grid c in {1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, inf} plus lower-only bounds {-2, -2.5, -3}; primary c = 2 (physical declaration); secondary nested c chosen in training folds (max inside R2 subject to coverage >= 0.7, one-SE toward wider). Arms B0, B1 (fold beta), HIST_D7; BPG decides, BP sensitivity; repeat at k = 4. Report coverage-R2 and coverage-MSE curves, coverage per cluster and pair type, inside/outside MSE ratio per cluster, LOCO, without C5-BTBP; read hull as a second axis. Controls at realised per-unit coverage (1,000 draws each): random, pair-type, cluster, pair type x cluster, publication-stratified. Window-aware Mondrian intervals (pair type x window) vs pair type alone, calibrated leave-one-cluster-out. Mechanism diagnostics with declared sign predictions and publication bootstrap: parity-signed chord vs level; chord sd vs minority-phase concentration; within-publication cross-extractant roughness in vs out. Apply the frozen rule to new sources.
kill_criterion: Killed if: inside R2 at c = 2 < 0.50; or nested inside R2 <= the 97.5 % quantile of the publication-stratified control (then it is a lab/data-quality flag, not a row flag); or LOCO minimum < 0.48; or inside/outside MSE ratio > 0.6 in more than a third of clusters with enough rows on both sides; or window-aware intervals are not >= 15 % narrower inside with per-cluster coverage >= 0.7; or a mechanism diagnostic shows a structured out-of-window signature outside C5-BTBP (tail modellable after all); or on new sources inside R2 < 0.45 or inside MSE not below outside.
expected_effect: Inside R2 about 0.52-0.55 at 67-80 % coverage; +0.03 to +0.05 over the publication-stratified control, about +0.08 over unstratified random; outside about 0.30; intervals roughly 40 % narrower inside. No all-row gain.
practical_value: A rule a chemist applies before trusting a 4-metal estimate: if predicted D of both metals is between 0.01 and 100, the adjacent-SF estimate is at the R2 0.54 / RMSE 0.14 level; otherwise measure the pair or move D into range via acidity, extractant concentration or phase ratio. Also a curation flag.
risks: Threshold history is post hoc; the domain partly encodes 'not C5-BTBP'; inside R2 is not comparable with 0.452 (state coverage); may add nothing on clean new data.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-3, statistics-3, physics-4; adds the full threshold curve, nested choice, publication-stratified decomposition, a physical a priori threshold, three mechanism checks already run, and window-aware intervals (gap G6).

title: Measure in the window: level-dependent reproducibility from sibling conditions, and a condition-choice rule
lens: measurement design (condition choice, detection-floor-aware design)
hypothesis: The tail of adjacent-SF irreproducibility sits where log D < about -3 (and partly > 2), mainly for light pairs. Same-extractant same-lab sibling conditions act as replicates and show this. Choosing conditions so the metals of interest have log D in about [-3, 2] makes measured SFs 2-4x more reproducible in the tail; reads-only flags (any read below L or above U) are a deployable domain.
rationale: Out-of-window rows hold about half of B1's SSE, and adjacent log SF is largely condition-invariant within a lab, so sibling disagreement measures how reliable a measured SF is at each level. This converts the error anatomy into a measurement instruction rather than a modelling target.
evidence_for: Sibling pairs (6,066 pair-rows, 20 publications): rms dSF 0.172 with all values in [-2, 2], 0.224 with any > 2, 0.329 with any < -2; by mean level <= -3 0.485, (-3, -2] 0.100; light pairs in vs out: Ce/Pr 0.193 vs 0.757, Sm/Eu 0.204 vs 0.398; heavy pairs unchanged; 7/11 publications out > in. Within-series roughness: robust sd 0.049 in vs 0.085 out, rms 0.110 vs 0.203 (0.302 at min <= -3); out > in in 15/20 extractant x publication groups (sign p 0.021); robust sd of condition-to-condition differences similar in and out, so the window adds outliers, not width. Reads-only flags: all reads in [-2, 2] 0.500 on 62 %; min read >= -2 0.500 on 83.5 %.
evidence_against: Effect is in the tail only, and the (-3, -2] band is the most consistent; confounded with publication (C5-BTBP supplies 986 out-of-window rows) and with extreme conditions where SF may truly change (loading, aggregation); no effect on heavy pairs; thresholds seen post hoc; the window depends on phase ratio and analytical method.
test_design: (a) Registered sibling-consistency analysis: within publication x extractant x pair type compare |dSF| for siblings with all values in [-3, 2], any < -3, any > 2; stratified permutation test (labels permuted within publication x pair type), publication-level sign test, trimmed and untrimmed rms; sensitivity without C5-BTBP. (b) Reads-only flags on the pre-declared grid L in {-3, -2.5, -2} x U in {2, 2.5, 3}: coverage-R2 for B0 and B1 against stratified random abstention at equal coverage (as in M09), per-cluster coverage, BPG deciding. (c) Supply the low-D arm of the repeatability campaign (M11).
kill_criterion: (a) Killed if the stratified permutation p > 0.05 for rms(< -3) > rms(in window), or fewer than 60 % of qualifying publications show out > in. (b) Killed if no pre-declared reads-only window beats random abstention by >= 0.03 R2 at >= 70 % coverage.
expected_effect: rms dSF ratio below -3 vs in window 1.5-2.5 (light pairs 2-4); reads-only window R2 0.50-0.54 at 60-85 % coverage vs about 0.45 random.
practical_value: Before relying on or reporting adjacent SF, adjust extractant concentration or acidity so the metals of interest have log D between about -3 and +2; process designers operate near log D 0 anyway. If any of the 4 reads is below -3, treat predicted light-pair SFs as unreliable.
risks: Window effects could be real chemistry; publication confounding with 20 publications; threshold selection; overlap with M09 (the new part is the measurement evidence and the condition-choice rule).
novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-5 (plus the within-series roughness check from acquisition-2); sibling consistency used as a replicate proxy, the tail-not-width finding, and a condition-choice rule.

title: Level-stratified repeatability campaign that settles the noise ceiling and the replicate-vs-add-a-metal trade-off
lens: measurement cost model + new data acquisition (H-CEILING campaign design)
hypothesis: In-window laboratory repeatability of adjacent log SF has a core sd <= 0.10, and the corpus's heavy tail comes from a gross-error component concentrated at floor and ceiling levels, so the projected sigma_SF on C3's level mix stays below the 0.157-0.19 threshold. Extra read noise of sd s costs about 0.22 s^2 of pair MSE at k = 3, so duplicating reads beats adding a 5th metal only above s of about 0.14-0.15.
rationale: The noise share of B1's MSE is known only to lie in [0.08, 0.87] (G1), and the ceiling threshold depends on the noise model (C10). A plain '6 systems x 3 runs at one condition' design would estimate the wrong quantity, because the out-of-window excess is a tail, not a uniformly larger sd. The same sigma decides whether labs should replicate or add metals.
evidence_for: Read-noise sensitivity (Gaussian noise on the 4 reads only, D7, k = 3): R2 0.451 / 0.447 / 0.440 / 0.429 / 0.407 / 0.351 at s = 0 / 0.03 / 0.05 / 0.07 / 0.10 / 0.15; dMSE/s^2 = 0.216-0.219; a legal 5th metal is worth +0.044-0.052. Noise handles: robust per-metal 0.030-0.058, mean-square 0.107-0.188, transcription replicate 0.049, double reports 0.086; replicate noise 54 % of B1's MSE on 15 cells. The out-of-window excess is in the rms, not in the robust sd (M10).
evidence_against: Six systems cannot pin a heterogeneous mean-square noise (replicated cells median 0.082 vs pooled 0.188; CV of pooled sigma^2 near 2 at n = 6); one lab measures repeatability, not reproducibility (M12); real noise is heavy-tailed (kurtosis 18.2); with ICP-MS all metals arrive together, so 'replicate vs add' becomes 'replicate vs new condition'; the five noisiest corpus replicate cells are DGA and three lie fully in window (possibly hidden-condition merges); the campaign needs lab access.
test_design: (a) Software now: read-noise sensitivity curve for B1 (fold refit) under DOPT_Q and BISECT at k = 3 and 4, Gaussian and t3 noise; simulated world (dense-read D7 truths plus resampled per-metal roughness, label and read noise independent) giving the replicate-vs-add break-even sigma and the sigma_SF at which 0.50 at k = 3 becomes impossible under the actual policy (resolves C10). (b) Data-gated campaign: about 6 systems spanning DGA, branched DGA, phenanthroline diamide, a low-D-prone N-donor, malonamide, organophosphorus; two conditions each (C_in set by a one-run pilot so all 14 Ln lie in [-1.5, 1.5]; C_low with the weak end near log D -3); 3 independent runs on different days with fresh stock and organic phase plus an analytical duplicate of every phase sample; both phases assayed (mass balance within 5 %); per-metal LOD/LOQ and oxide ratios; metals <= 0.1 mM each; optionally a second operator or lab. Analysis: run-offset removal; REML variance components (analytical / run / lab); core-plus-gross-error mixture per condition; projection sigma^2 = 0.747 sigma_in^2 + 0.253 sigma_out^2; ceilings 1 - sigma^2/0.0493 and 1 - 0.67 sigma^2/0.0493. Freeze model, policy and thresholds before any value arrives.
kill_criterion: (a) If the simulated break-even sigma lies outside [0.03, 0.19] under both noise shapes, the trade-off is moot (always add metals) and the analytical-repeat arm is dropped. (b) In-window core sigma_SF with lower 90 % bound >= 0.157 (or >= the simulated threshold): 0.50 at k = 3 declared noise-bound, switch to replicate-mean targets or wider pairs. Projected upper bound < 0.12 (or sigma_SF <= 0.10): the shortfall is a modelling or curation problem. Gross-error rate out >= 2x in and rms ratio >= 2: the window is adopted a priori. Otherwise extend by 3 systems.
expected_effect: In-window core sigma_SF about 0.06-0.09 (ceiling 0.84-0.93); out-of-window gross-error rate several times higher; break-even about 0.14-0.15, so 'add metals' usually wins.
practical_value: A stated precision for adjacent SF measured in window vs near the floor; a one-line rule on whether to repeat a determination or add a metal; the deciding experiment on whether 0.50 at k = 3 is a modelling or a measurement target; variance components for the confirmation power studies (M36).
risks: Pilot uses measured levels (legitimate for design; log it); labs may report only means (insist on per-run data); third-phase or loading effects; projection assumes the corpus level mix and mechanism; simulator realism.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-2, measurement-6; level-stratified two-condition design with a core-plus-gross mixture, a measured replicate-vs-add exchange rate, and a policy-specific simulated threshold, versus round 3's single-condition repeat request.

title: Inter-laboratory reproducibility of adjacent log SF: matched-condition literature meta-analysis first, ring test second
lens: meta-analysis of laboratory effects + balanced reproducibility campaign
hypothesis: The programme's cross-publication failure is either a laboratory signature (labs measure different adjacent SF for the same system and condition; roughness reproduces within lab, not between) or condition mismatch (labs agree at matched conditions, between-lab tau^2 <= 0.005). Two staged measurements decide between them.
rationale: Every cross-source null of rounds 1-4 has these two readings. H-CEILING targets within-lab repeatability only; between-lab reproducibility has never been estimated, yet it bounds every BP/BPG model, decides whether the publication is a valid confirmation unit, and decides whether the sibling gain transfers to a user's own lab.
evidence_for: Matched-condition, different-publication pairs: MSE 0.021 (5 pairs) vs unmatched 0.048 (835) vs same-publication matched 0.030. Within a lab, copy error rises with |dlog acid| (rho +0.30). Roughness r +0.36 / +0.14 / -0.02; cross-publication copy R2 -0.08; hidden heavy-metal mean level errors all positive (consistent with, not proof of, an analytical bias); the archive records no analytical method.
evidence_against: Five matched pairs are an anecdote; level-nearest cross-publication templates still fail (0.164 vs 0.499); the oxide-interference model was no better than placebo (M06); a ring test is costly and labs may harmonise informally; matched replicates may be too rare to find.
test_design: Stage 1 (software plus literature; needs the user's access, no downloads without permission): count matched cross-publication pairs per system in master_clean and V1 under pre-declared tolerances (same acid type, |dlog acid| <= 0.1, |dlog L| <= 0.1, same diluent class); harvest independent measurements of the systems with most labs (tables and SI first; figures only through M22's verified digitisation); random-effects model per pair type with condition strata; report tau^2, I^2 and the implied cross-source cap; analysis plan frozen before any harvested value is read. Stage 2 (if Stage 1 has < 30 comparisons from >= 6 labs or is inconclusive): 2 systems (a TODGA reference and a phenanthroline diamide) x 4 labs x 3 runs at one SOP placing all Ln in log D [-1.5, 1.5]; shared extractant batch and feed plus one own-feed run; raw intensities, isotopes, interference corrections and LOD reported; variance components; within- vs between-lab roughness correlation (12 lab-pair x system comparisons); reprocessing with and without interference correction.
kill_criterion: Lab signature supported (close cross-source modelling together with M08; lab becomes the confirmation unit; sibling regime same-lab only) if tau^2 >= 0.02 with lower bound > 0.01, or between-lab roughness r < 0.15 with within-lab r >= 0.30. Lab-bias explanation killed (condition-matched cross-lab regime and condition-aware cross-publication models reopened; publication unit downgraded) if tau^2 <= 0.005, or between-lab r >= 0.30 with sigma_between <= 1.2 sigma_within. Stage 1 is uninformative if < 30 matched comparisons from >= 6 labs exist.
expected_effect: The first number for inter-laboratory reproducibility of adjacent log SF and an explicit upper bound on any BP/BPG model; prior leans toward a laboratory signature.
practical_value: How far to trust a literature adjacent SF from another lab for the user's system; an inter-lab uncertainty to carry into stage-count calculations (for SF 1.2-1.5 a 0.1-log spread changes stage counts materially); whether interference corrections must be reported with published SFs.
risks: Scarce matched replicates; publication bias toward agreement; incomplete condition metadata; recruiting labs is slow; results for two systems may not generalise.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-5, contrarian-6; reproducibility (not repeatability) across labs, staged from a cheap desk meta-analysis to a ring test with an analytical-interference control.

title: Group-cut estimand: wider pairs (dZ = 2-4, including Nd/Sm) from the same 4 reads, against a slope-only LINE and a read-free prior
lens: regime / estimand reframing (cut points instead of strict neighbours)
hypothesis: For dZ = 2-4 pairs (including Nd/Sm, adjacent in real feeds because Pm is absent), the same 4 DOPT_Q reads give R2 >= 0.65 with B1's form, and the skill is read-anchored interpolation, not slope: B1 beats a 2-parameter LINE through the reads by >= 0.15 and a read-free pair-type prior by >= 0.5. Registered separately; never pooled with the strict-adjacent target.
rationale: Strict-adjacent pairs have the lowest signal-to-roughness ratio: per-metal roughness is fixed while signal grows with dZ. Many process decisions are about where to cut a series. The cheapest sensible alternative is LINE; if it matched B1, the claim would only be 'amplitude'.
evidence_against: Higher R2 partly reflects 2.2-5x larger var(y); absolute MAE is larger than for strict pairs; wider pairs share hidden metals with the main rows (correlated estimand); substitution trap: pooling strict pairs with Nd/Sm gives 0.551; exploratory numbers use the fixed -0.072.
test_design: Separate estimand E-W: all pairs with dZ in {2, 3, 4} and >= 1 end unread at k = 3 DOPT_Q, V1 C3, BPG deciding, BP sensitivity. Arms B0, B1 (fold-refit beta), HIST_D7, LINE, RIDGE2, HBK@ML, pair-type prior, G14 zero-shot where defined, FLAT. Report per pair type R2, MAE and sign agreement; pooled within dZ class plus a macro-average over pair types; a pre-declared cut-pair set (Nd/Sm, Eu/Tb, Gd/Dy, Dy/Er). Contrasts B1 - LINE and B1 - prior with cluster bootstrap and LOCO; read ladder 2-4. 'Strict + Nd/Sm' only as its own labelled row.
kill_criterion: Killed or narrowed if B1 - LINE on dZ = 2 < +0.10 or its cluster lower bound <= 0 (claim narrows to 'amplitude alone'), Nd/Sm B1 R2 < 0.65, or macro per-pair-type R2 for dZ = 2 < 0.50.
expected_effect: dZ = 2 about 0.65-0.68 (macro slightly lower), +0.2 over LINE; Nd/Sm about 0.75; dZ = 3-4 about 0.80; strict-adjacent stays 0.452.
practical_value: Cut-point selectivities (light | middle at Nd/Sm, inside the middle group, middle | heavy) can be estimated from 4 metals with R2 about 0.7-0.8 and sign agreement 0.80-0.88; LINE or family priors do much worse. Strict-adjacent purification still needs measurement or a sibling series (M01).
risks: Readers may treat it as a model improvement; correlated rows; the process-adjacent label must not be used to redefine adjacency after the fact.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-4; adds the LINE and prior controls, a macro metric, a declared cut-pair set, and quantifies the substitution trap.

title: Decision estimand: risk-controlled direction and separability calls with abstain-to-measure, plus net-benefit decision curves
lens: decision endpoints (selective prediction with risk control; decision-curve analysis)
hypothesis: With thresholds on B1's |prediction| calibrated on training folds, B1 issues direction calls on >= 50 % of strict-adjacent pairs at <= 10 % false-sign, where LINE, zero-shot G14 and a pair-type prior can issue <= 10 % at the same risk. B1's recalibrated P(|log SF| >= 0.3) gives positive net benefit over treat-all, treat-none, the prior and G14 at thresholds 0.2-0.5, also outside the dominant cluster. At full coverage B1 has no direction advantage over LINE; its value is knowing which pairs it can call.
rationale: A chemist does not consume R2; they decide which pairs to trust and which candidate systems deserve a full study, at some error budget or cost ratio. Prior reports gave selective accuracy at ad hoc cut-offs without calibrated thresholds or matched-risk baselines.
evidence_for: alpha = 0.10 (coverage / realised false-sign): B1 0.606 / 0.107; B0 0.508 / 0.099; LINE 0.086 / 0.118; G14 0.013 / 0.252; prior 0.032 / 0.312. alpha = 0.05: B1 0.257 / 0.068. Large clusters near nominal at alpha 0.10 (giant 0.096, phenanthroline 0.097). Net benefit at p_t 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5: B1 0.079 / 0.061 / 0.031; G14 0.052 / 0.005 / -0.001; prior 0.046 / -0.001 / 0; non-dominant clusters B1 0.090 / 0.075 / 0.049. Brier 0.103 vs 0.130 / 0.128. Three-class separability 0.652 vs majority 0.459.
evidence_against: At full coverage LINE's direction accuracy (0.744) is at least B1's (0.732) when zeros count as errors; cluster-conditional validity fails at alpha 0.10 (BTBP cluster 0.174, another 0.225) and neither Mondrian thresholds nor the window fix it; realised 0.068 at nominal 0.05; no net-benefit gain at p_t 0.1; calibration slope 0.77 (overconfident); a level-normalised conformal variant did not help.
test_design: Registered E-DEC on V1 C3, k = 3, DOPT_Q; BPG decides, BP sensitivity. Conformal risk control: thresholds on |p| fitted on training folds only, alpha in {0.10, 0.05}; Mondrian by pair type as secondary. Arms at matched risk: B1 (fold beta), B0, LINE, RIDGE2, G14, pair-type sign prior. Endpoints: coverage at risk alpha and realised false-sign, pooled, per cluster, per pair type and within |y| >= 0.1; three-class separability (< 0.1, 0.1-0.3, >= 0.3) with risk-controlled abstention at 0.2 misclassification; P(SF >= 2) from cross-fold pair-type residual distributions with Platt recalibration on other folds; net benefit at p_t {0.2, 0.3, 0.5} for 'separable' and 'inseparable' decisions vs treat-all/none; calibration slope per cluster; measurements saved. Cluster bootstrap for coverage and net-benefit differences; frozen thresholds applied to any new source.
kill_criterion: Killed if: pooled realised false-sign > alpha + 0.03; or B1 coverage minus the best baseline < 0.20 at alpha 0.10; or the giant or phenanthroline cluster has realised rate > 2 alpha; or delta net benefit vs the best comparator has a 90 % interval including 0 at >= 2 of 3 thresholds; or the recalibrated slope is outside [0.8, 1.25] in non-dominant clusters; or on new sources the realised rate > 0.15 at nominal 0.10. Failure in small clusters only forces a marginal-only claim.
expected_effect: About 55-60 % of pairs called at about 10 % false-sign, about 25 % at 6-7 %; best non-read baseline <= 10 %; delta net benefit +0.03 to +0.06 at p_t 0.3; pooled R2 unchanged.
practical_value: For a new extractant measured at 4 metals, the model says which adjacent pairs it can sign with about 90 % reliability and gives a calibrated P(SF >= 2) per pair, with the cost-ratio range in which to use it; the remaining pairs go to direct measurement.
risks: Could look like endpoint switching unless registered up front; cluster-conditional failure already visible; low-|y| calls matter less (report |y| >= 0.1); never present as an R2 gain.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-5, contrarian-4; calibrated risk control with matched-risk baselines, the full-coverage correction, net-benefit curves with explicit cost thresholds, and a cluster-conditional calibration audit.

title: Screening estimand for ranking candidates from partial series, with a slope-only LINE control
lens: ranking / screening decision endpoint
hypothesis: When choosing the most selective of about 18 candidate extractants for a declared adjacent pair from 4-read partial series, B1's advantage over random is mostly the cell's amplitude: LINE through the same reads recovers >= 80 % of B1's regret reduction, 2 reads recover >= 50 %, and zero-shot models are at chance. The claim is expected to narrow to 'screening = amplitude from >= 3 spread reads'.
rationale: Ranking skill had been reported without a slope control or k ladder. If LINE matches B1, a chemist mining partial literature data needs no interpolation model, only reads that span the series.
evidence_for: 288 seed x fold x pair-type groups, median 18 candidates: top-1 / regret B1 0.281 / 0.219; PWL_R 0.271 / 0.222; LINE 0.250 / 0.250; G14 0.073 / 0.398; random 0.061 / 0.394. LINE recovers 82 % of B1's regret reduction. 2 reads: D7 / LINE top-1 0.191 / 0.191; 3 reads 0.247 / 0.243. Within-cell ranking Spearman B1 0.585 vs prior 0.393 vs G14 0.353.
evidence_against: If both ends of the target pair can be measured, measurement dominates (meaningful only for fixed partial data); candidate groups sit inside test folds (dominant fold 58 % of rows); top-1 is noisy with about 18 candidates; DOPT_Q read sets are not what papers report.
test_design: Registered E-RANK: per seed, fold and pair type with >= 5 test candidates, rank by |p|. Endpoints top-1, top-3, regret (log units), Spearman(|p|, |y|). Arms B1, B0, LINE, RIDGE2, HBK@ML, G14, random expectation. Read ladder 2-4 (DOPT_Q nested). Literature-mining sensitivity: read sets resampled from the empirical metal subsets of V1's partial cells where legal. Primary contrast B1 - LINE on regret with cluster bootstrap, plus the share of B1's regret reduction LINE recovers.
kill_criterion: Interpolation-specific claim dies if B1 - LINE regret improvement < 0.02 log with a cluster interval including 0 (conclusion: screening skill = amplitude). Whole screening claim dies if B1 top-1 < 0.20, or regret not below random by >= 0.10 under BPG, or it fails the observational-read-set sensitivity.
expected_effect: B1 top-1 about 0.28, regret about 0.22; B1 - LINE about 0.03 log, probably not significant; 2 reads lose about a third of top-1; zero-shot at chance.
practical_value: For shortlisting extractants from partial literature series: any 3-4 reads spanning the series give about 4.5x the random top-1 rate and nearly halve regret; a slope fit does almost as well; structure-only screening is useless; if the pair is measurable, measure it.
risks: Likely a narrowing, not a gain; small noisy groups; depends on the assumed read-set distribution.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-6; adds the LINE control (82 %), the read ladder for ranking, and the literature-mining framing with an observational read-set sensitivity.

title: Publication-balanced (two-layer) conformal intervals and certified decision rates for a new laboratory
lens: conformal / selective prediction under laboratory random effects
hypothesis: Split-conformal intervals for B1 calibrated on a CDF that gives each publication equal weight (two-layer hierarchical exchangeability), combined with Mondrian pair-type strata, give near-nominal coverage for an unseen laboratory (every cluster >= 0.85 at 90 %) at <= 35 % extra width, with honest certified direction calls (accuracy >= 0.95 among calls).
rationale: Row-exchangeable conformal calibrates to the giant cluster and under-covers new sources (0.754 at 80 % outside it; per-cluster 0.52-1.00). Group-balanced calibration is the standard remedy when the test unit is a new group; a deployable interval matters more to a chemist than a 0.01 R2 gain.
evidence_for: At 90 %: row-weighted Mondrian coverage 0.893, min cluster 0.62, 24 % of publications under-covered by > 10 points, half-width 0.244; publication-weighted 0.921, min 0.82, 8 %, 0.314 (+29 %); cluster-weighted 0.913, 0.73, 13 %, 0.289. Rest-of-corpus coverage at 80 % rises from 0.754 to 0.809.
evidence_against: At 80 % min cluster coverage goes 0.52 -> 0.48 and width 0.151 -> 0.189 (weak); window strata do not lift the worst cluster; certification is nearly unattainable: a publication-weighted bound on direction error <= 5 % admits 0.5 % of rows, and 90 % intervals exclude 0 on 11.7 % of rows with accuracy 0.923; 1/n_pub weights let tiny publications dominate; 13 clusters make per-cluster estimates noisy.
test_design: BPG folds decide; leave-one-cluster-out (13 folds) as sensitivity. Calibration scores = |B1 residual| of training-fold OOF rows only. Variants: R row-weighted, M Mondrian by pair type, P publication-weighted, PM, C cluster-weighted, S Dunn-Wasserman-Ramdas subsampling (one row per publication, 500 draws). Finite-sample quantile correction; nominal 80 % and 90 %. Outcomes: marginal coverage, per-cluster minimum and count below nominal - 0.05, share of publications (>= 25 rows) under-covered by > 10 points, mean half-width, Winkler score, per fold type. Decision endpoints with realised accuracy: certified direction, certified SF >= 2 (lower bound > 0.30), certified inseparable (interval within +-0.1). Control: same variants on HBK@ML.
kill_criterion: Killed if PM's minimum per-cluster coverage at 90 % under leave-one-cluster-out < 0.80, or PM's half-width > 1.5x R's, or its Winkler score is worse than R's by > 10 %, or certified-direction accuracy < 0.93.
expected_effect: Coverage 0.91-0.93 at 90 %; min cluster 0.78-0.85 (vs 0.62); width +25-35 %; certified direction on about 10-15 % of rows at accuracy about 0.92-0.95.
practical_value: A chemist from a new laboratory gets an interval that holds for their kind of source (about a factor of 2 in SF at 90 %) and a plain statement that from 4 metals only about 1 adjacent pair in 8 can be certified; the rest need measurement.
risks: 13 clusters with one at 65 %; publications not strictly exchangeable (copy groups, shared labs); heavy-tailed scores destabilise the 90 % quantile; certified rates may be too small to matter.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: statistics-2; first group-balanced calibration and first test of whether interval-based decisions can be certified for a new laboratory.

title: Pair-resolved read-policy crossing: hull-closing BISECT moves skill from the light end to the heavy end
lens: measurement design (read placement), pair-type endpoints
hypothesis: At k = 3 the label-free extremes-first BISECT policy barely moves pooled R2 over DOPT_Q but makes Yb/Lu and Tm/Yb predictable while costing Ce/Pr. A pair-resolved endpoint (macro mean of the 12 per-pair R2, heavy- and light-block R2) detects this with cluster intervals excluding 0; hull closure, not roughness weighting, is the lever.
rationale: Error does not grow with distance to the nearest read; what matters is which metal is hidden and whether a pair lies outside the read hull (11.9 % of rows, R2 about 0). DOPT_Q reads Lu in only about 14 % of cells. With 4 reads a policy is really a choice of target block, so it should be declared and scored that way (resolves C5/C6).
evidence_for: Pooled 0.451 -> 0.462 (+0.011, cluster bootstrap [-0.013, +0.035]). Yb/Lu 0.002 -> 0.488 ([+0.318, +0.804], LOCO [+0.466, +0.523]); Tm/Yb 0.026 -> 0.206; Sm/Eu 0.43 -> 0.61; Tb/Dy 0.36 -> 0.53; heavy block +0.121; macro +0.067 ([+0.041, +0.165]). BISECT reads Lu in 73 % of cells (DOPT_Q 14 %) and Gd in 35 % (61 %), the hindsight oracle's direction. A roughness-weighted policy scores 0.249 without hull closure and 0.458 with it.
evidence_against: Ce/Pr 0.419 -> 0.274 ([-0.236, -0.084]); Eu/Gd -0.083; Er/Tm -0.06. The pooled gain sits mostly in the 51 kmax = 3 cells (+0.005 elsewhere); at k = 4-5 BISECT is about equal to DOPT_Q and wins only at k = 6; the minimal hull edit of DOPT_Q gives only +0.003; BISECT was already seen; fixed beta; per-pair R2 on 125-176 rows per seed; heavy pairs carry only 8.6 % of SSE.
test_design: Policy crossing on identical legal queries, BPG deciding, BP sensitivity. Policies: DOPT_Q; BISECT; HULL-DOPT (heaviest DOPT_Q read replaced by the heaviest legal metal); LIGHT-GUARD (pre-declared: BISECT with the 3rd read forced to the second-lightest legal metal); random legal floor. Predictors B0, B1 with beta refit per fold on each policy's reads, HIST_D7. Budgets k = 1-6. Endpoints: pooled R2 (non-inferiority margin -0.01 vs DOPT_Q), macro per-pair R2, heavy-block and light-block R2, Yb/Lu R2, balanced MAE. Cluster_cpg bootstrap (2,000) and LOCO; split by fold type and by kmax = 3 vs >= 4. Compare with model-side damped edge continuation (M28) for extrapolated rows.
kill_criterion: Heavy-end claim killed if BISECT's heavy-block gain over DOPT_Q under BPG with B1 refit is < +0.05 or its lower bound <= 0. BISECT not adopted as reference if pooled R2 < DOPT_Q - 0.01 or LIGHT-GUARD cannot keep Ce/Pr within -0.05 of DOPT_Q. Per-block recommendations stand only where the block interval excludes 0.
expected_effect: Pooled +0.005 to +0.011 (not decisive); macro pair R2 +0.05 to +0.07; Yb/Lu +0.3 to +0.5; Tm/Yb +0.1 to +0.2; light block -0.05 to -0.10 unless LIGHT-GUARD recovers it.
practical_value: A chemist who cares about heavy pairs (Yb/Lu, Tm/Yb, Er/Tm) must measure the heaviest metal; without it the predicted heavy SF is no better than 'no separation'. One who cares about Ce/Pr/Nd should keep DOPT_Q-type sets that include Pr. The programme gets a per-block policy rule instead of choosing policies by pooled R2.
risks: Post hoc (BISECT and the hull edit seen); 13 clusters; small heavy-pair variance means large R2 changes are small absolute errors; a block policy needs a user who declares a target block.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-1; per-pair crossing with cluster intervals, Lu/Gd read frequencies set against the oracle, kmax decomposition of the pooled gain, and the hull-edit and roughness-prior controls.

title: Metals-to-0.50 on fixed cohorts: the apparent 5-metal crossing on C3 is a cohort-mixture effect
lens: measurement design (k ladder) with like-for-like cohorts
hypothesis: On cells that can actually take extra legal reads, B1 reaches adjacent R2 0.50 only at 6 measured metals (k = 5). The C3 figure of about 0.50 at 5 metals arises because the 51 cells that cannot take a 5th read keep their (easy) k = 3 predictions.
rationale: H-BUDGET ranks second because its estimate sits on 0.50. A C3 ladder row mixes 178 cells scored at k = 4 with 51 cells still at k = 3. The honest 'how many metals' answer must come from fixed cohorts scored at every rung.
evidence_for: C3 with k = min(K, kmax), DOPT_Q / BISECT: K = 4 0.496 / 0.501; K = 5 0.529 / 0.534; K = 6 0.550 / 0.572. Fixed cohorts: C4 K = 3 0.429 / 0.434, K = 4 0.479 / 0.478; C5 K = 4 0.482, K = 5 0.522 / 0.518; C6 K = 5 0.524 / 0.520, K = 6 0.552 / 0.571. The 51 kmax = 3 cells score 0.597 / 0.650 at k = 3 vs 0.429 / 0.434 for kmax >= 4. Consistent with E3 (max-min 5th read 0.503, 3/5 seeds) and E6 (C6 crosses at k = 5).
evidence_against: Beta fixed at -0.072, not refit (gap G3; shift about 0.001-0.005); fixed cohorts are harder than C3, so cohort difficulty and read count are confounded; legality forbids reading a strict neighbour while real labs get measured pairs; BISECT figures come from a policy seen post hoc.
test_design: Registered E-D ladder. Primary: for each K = 1-6 a fixed nested cohort C_K (cells with kmax >= K) scored at every k <= K on identical queries. Secondary: the C3 min(K, kmax) row. Policies DOPT_Q-nested (primary) and BISECT (secondary). Predictors B0, B1 (beta refit per fold and per k, BPG and BP), HIST_D7. Report seed range, cluster bootstrap, LOCO, kmax strata (3, 4-5, 6), balanced MAE, and P(R2 >= 0.50) with interval (M38) rather than pass/fail. Pre-declared k* = smallest K with fixed-cohort B1 >= 0.50 in >= 4/5 BPG seeds. Like-for-like control: C3 at k = 3 restricted to C4 cells.
kill_criterion: Hypothesis killed ('5 metals suffice') if fixed-cohort C4 with refit B1 reaches >= 0.50 at K = 4 in >= 4/5 BPG seeds. Mixture explanation killed if, with B1 refit, kmax = 3 cells do not exceed kmax >= 4 cells by >= 0.10 R2 at the same k.
expected_effect: Fixed-cohort R2: K = 4 about 0.475-0.485; K = 5 about 0.515-0.525; K = 6 about 0.55-0.57 (BISECT about +0.02 at K = 6); k* = 5, i.e. 6 measured metals, cluster lower bound near 0.48.
practical_value: The honest budget statement for subset feeds and literature gap-filling: 4 metals give about 0.43-0.45 on a typical >= 10-metal series; 5 metals is a coin flip; 6 metals spaced every other one including both ends give 0.52-0.57. A '0.50 at 5 metals on C3' claim would be an artefact of small easy cells.
risks: The 0.50 target is arbitrary; cohort definitions depend on the legality model; with 13 clusters the crossing interval will straddle 0.50 whatever happens (the deliverable is the curve).
novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-2; kmax-mixture decomposition, fixed-cohort C4/C5 rungs and a BISECT ladder that reframe H-BUDGET.

title: Value of the next measurement across a screening set: allocate extra reads between cells, not between metals
lens: measurement design (adaptive budget allocation across candidates)
hypothesis: The SSE reduction from a 5th read is predictable between cells from label-free read features, even though it is not within a cell. Allocating half the extra reads to cells with the largest predicted adjacent-SF mass (sum of |B1 predicted log SF|) captures most of the full-budget gain and beats random and size-only allocation.
rationale: B1's error concentrates in cells with a wide spread of SFs (Spearman of cell MSE with cell sd of y 0.91). A screening campaign or literature gap-filling spends its budget across extractants, so the useful question is which extractant gets the next measurement, not which metal (the latter is nearly unlearnable).
evidence_for: Spearman(score, SSE drop): predicted-SF mass 0.55 (DOPT_Q-nested) / 0.60 (max-min); read range x hidden count 0.51 / 0.58; size only 0.44 / 0.42. Max-min 5th read on 50 % of eligible cells: score 0.4914, random 0.4771, size-only 0.4850, oracle 0.5027, all cells 0.5030 (from 0.4511), so half the reads deliver 78 % of the gain; score - random +0.014 [+0.002, +0.031], LOCO [+0.007, +0.019]; score - size +0.006 [-0.004, +0.033]. DOPT_Q-nested: 0.4819 vs 0.4734 vs oracle 0.4956.
evidence_against: Score picked among 9 tried; most of the gain is cell size (+0.008 of +0.014) and the spread part over size has an interval including 0; fixed beta; large-|SF| cells are also where tail noise lives; moot with ICP-MS where all metals come together.
test_design: Registered E-G, no training. Primary score: sum over adjacent pairs of |B1 predicted log SF| at k = 3 (B1 fold refit); secondary read range x hidden count. Budgets {0.25, 0.5} of eligible cells. Next read DOPT_Q-nested (primary) and max-min (secondary). Arms: score, size-only, random (exact expectation), oracle allocation. Endpoint pooled R2 at fixed total reads with balanced MAE guard; BPG decides; cluster bootstrap and LOCO; with and without C5-BTBP.
kill_criterion: Killed at the 50 % budget under BPG with B1 refit if score - random < +0.005 R2, or score <= size-only + 0.002, or the score - random cluster lower bound <= 0.
expected_effect: At 50 % budget: +0.008 to +0.015 over random, +0.003 to +0.006 over size-only.
practical_value: When screening 10-30 extractants where each extra metal costs a separate determination or literature search: after 4 metals each, spend the next measurement on extractants with the largest predicted adjacent SFs; half the extra measurements give about 80 % of the benefit.
risks: Partly 'measure the big cells' (size-only control must be shown); large-SF floor cells may make the gain partly noise; only one pre-declared score.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-4; between-cell allocation and its exchange rate with random and size-only allocation were never evaluated (only within-cell adaptive choice).

title: Unmeasurable-end scenario: predict the two adjacent SFs of a metal that cannot be measured, from its measured neighbours
lens: measurement design (pair-targeted reads, the stated scenario for gap G8)
hypothesis: When a laboratory cannot measure one metal but measures both its Z-neighbours, radius interpolation predicts that metal's two adjacent SFs with the accuracy of the bench's isolated-hidden-metal analogues (R2 about 0.55, MAE about 0.11 log, direction about 0.8). External series in which that metal was measured decide between plain radius interpolation and a tetrad-boundary kink.
rationale: Pair-targeted reads win 12/12 pair types, but a lab able to read one end can usually read the other, so G8 asks for a scenario where one end cannot be measured. A metal without a stable isotope, bracketed by two routinely measured neighbours, is that scenario and the cleanest geometry available.
evidence_for: Bench proxy (middle metal predicted from both neighbours, all V1 cells): hidden Pr R2 0.542, MAE 0.114, direction 0.843 (0.898 for |y| >= 0.1); hidden Eu 0.559 / 0.111 / 0.794; Dy 0.692; Ho 0.556; Tm 0.462; Er 0.287. Per-metal table split-half reliability 0.79 [0.55, 0.94]. Isolated hidden metals with a 2-Z bracket give 0.539 (E2).
evidence_against: The archive has essentially no data for the motivating metal, so validation depends on external series, which are mostly acidic organophosphorus systems while C3 is mostly DGA; the metal sits at a tetrad boundary (the Nd dip shows the neighbour chord is chemistry-dependent); external data come from a different measurement technique with different noise.
test_design: (a) Bench, training-free, registered: an 'unmeasurable middle metal' estimand for every interior metal, scored on its two adjacent SFs; arms radius interpolation, Z interpolation and a pre-declared tetrad-kink variant; chemotype and cluster bootstrap; Gd handled with B1's term. (b) Desk validation (web reading only, no downloads; closed papers need the user): pre-register extraction rules and scoring before reading values; compile series with the target metal and both neighbours under one condition (target >= 8 series from >= 4 labs); report MAE, direction and the sign of the deviation from the neighbour chord (tests the tetrad reading, C8).
kill_criterion: (a) Killed if the light-analogue (Pr, Eu) proxy R2 has a cluster lower bound < 0.40 or direction accuracy < 0.75. (b) Killed (proxy only, not offered to users) if the median |error| of the predicted level exceeds the median |adjacent SF|, or fewer than 4 independent external series exist.
expected_effect: Proxy R2 0.50-0.56, direction about 0.8; 3-8 external series; a systematic deviation would favour the tetrad reading of the Nd dip.
practical_value: Lets a chemist estimate selectivity involving a metal they cannot handle from cold measurements of its neighbours, and gives the programme the concrete one-end-unmeasurable scenario G8 asked for.
risks: The proxy is not the target metal; small chemotype-skewed validation set; figure-read values carry transcription noise.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-7; the isolated-middle accuracy table with reliability, a stated unmeasurable-end scenario, and an external test that also bears on the Nd-dip origin.

title: Provenance class (figure-digitised / table / no location) as a frozen, label-free reporting axis
lens: data quality and provenance (reporting stratum)
hypothesis: The archive's data_location class is label-free metadata that strongly modifies B1's difficulty and its Gd gain: figure-digitised series are smoother with a weaker Gd dip, and B1's gain lives almost entirely in table and no-location cells, so the pooled 0.452 averages three different benchmarks.
rationale: Every round-4 verdict was read from one pooled number mixing curves a digitiser smoothed, primary numeric tables and coarse imports. A class map is metadata, so it can be frozen before any round-5 result and used to show which class carries each verdict.
evidence_for: FIG: 98 cells, 1 cluster, 37.5 % of rows, 20.2 % of SSE, MSE 0.0146, B1 0.511 vs B0 0.520 (Gd term -0.0095). TAB: 43 cells, MSE 0.0236, B1 0.339 vs 0.284. NONE: 80 cells, 12 of 13 clusters, 59.5 % of SSE, holds 2.29 of B1's 3.02 SSE/seed gain. Within sc009: B1 - B0 -0.015 FIG / +0.030 TAB / +0.056 NONE; median |second difference| 0.038 / 0.065 / 0.074; fitted Gd amplitude -0.040 / -0.116 / -0.163. S02's round-4 loss: +11.3 % SSE on documented cells vs -0.36 % on no-location cells.
evidence_against: Class is almost collinear with source cluster (FIG is the giant cluster only); only 5 TAB publications; FIG is mostly sc009 whose real dip is weak, so the effect may be chemistry, not digitisation (TODGA FIG -0.047 vs TAB -0.063, small); a documented-only domain keeps only 3 clusters and is not usable.
test_design: 1. Freeze a class map before any round-5 scoring (regex on data_location per cell x metal; cell class or MIXED with a declared rule), stored with an LF digest. 2. For B0, B1 and every round-5 candidate on V1 C3 k = 3 DOPT_Q, BPG deciding, report per class: R2, dSSE % vs B1, B1 - B0, cluster counts. 3. Lead sub-test (exploratory): within sc009, FIG - TAB difference in per-row B1 - B0 dSSE, publication bootstrap (15 publications, 2,000 draws) and a permutation of class labels among whole publications (1,000). 4. Within-publication check on the 3 publications with both FIG and TAB cells and the 12 two-location cells. Class-conditional models forbidden unless pre-registered with a power study.
kill_criterion: Provenance kept only as a descriptive table if the within-sc009 FIG - TAB difference has a publication-bootstrap 95 % CI including 0 and permutation p > 0.10 (then provenance is just publication), or if FIG/TAB roughness differs by less than a factor 1.3 within sc009.
expected_effect: No E-A gain (reporting axis). Expected readout: B1 about 0.51 FIG, 0.34 TAB, 0.43 NONE; Gd gain about 0 on FIG and about +0.05 on TAB/NONE; the within-sc009 contrast likely positive but under-powered.
practical_value: A chemist predicting from primary numeric tables should expect TAB/NONE-like accuracy (R2 0.34-0.48), not 0.45 or 0.51, and keep the Gd correction; reads from digitised literature figures are smoother. Raises the priority of source recovery for the 12 non-giant clusters, which carry all cross-chemotype evidence.
risks: Class map built after seeing the cells (class-specific claims are leads); MIXED cells need a declared rule.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-1; the data_location class, the sign flip of B1's Gd gain on figure cells, per-class roughness and Gd amplitude, and the provenance split of S02's loss are new.

title: Figure-versus-table digitisation calibration as a gate: attenuation of single-metal features, digitisation accuracy, then verified figure mining for new independent sources
lens: data quality (measurement-process bias) + LLM-assisted extraction with verification
