hypothesis: Re-digitising published figures whose data also exist as tables measures (i) whether digitisation attenuates single-metal features such as the Gd dip (slope < 1) and (ii) the digitisation error of adjacent log SF. If the error sd is <= 0.05 with no material attenuation, double extraction (LLM vision plus a manual digitiser) of the figure-only literature can add >= 30 new independent source clusters and lift confirmation power from <= 0.10 to a usable level.
rationale: FIG cells are markedly smoother with a weaker Gd dip (M21); that is either chemistry or a digitisation artefact, with opposite advice for primary data. Separately, confirmation needs 40-80 new sources while table-based supply is 3-5, and many lanthanide-series papers publish only figures. Both questions are answered by the same calibration experiment, which must pass before figure data are used as reads, labels or confirmation.
evidence_for: FIG vs TAB median |second difference| 0.028 vs 0.049 (within sc009 0.038 vs 0.065); raw Gd dip -0.049 vs -0.093; fitted Gd amplitude -0.040 vs -0.116. In one two-location cell, figure and table differ by -1.10 at La to -0.04 at Gd (light-end-specific). Adjacent-SF disagreement between two data locations of one cell: median 0.025 (two tables), 0.050 (two figures), 0.119 (figure vs table). But by B1 error figure cells are not rougher (MSE 0.016 vs 0.024; within DGA 0.0159 vs 0.0262; publication-level p 0.78), so plotted sources look admissible. Transcription replicate sd 0.049; confirmation power 0.04 / 0.10 / 0.27 at G = 5 / 10 / 40.
evidence_against: FIG cells concentrate in TODGA-type chemistry with a plausibly weak dip; two-location cells are mostly hidden-condition merges; log-axis digitising is usually accurate to 0.01-0.02 decades; an adjacent SF from two digitised points inflates error by sqrt(2); LLM vision can hallucinate coordinates; new figure sources may again be DGA (no Kish gain); copyright and access need the user.
test_design: Phase 1 (user-supplied PDFs; numbers stored, not figures): >= 20 V1 cells whose paper gives the same data as table and figure (corpus papers first; never open-access papers reserved for confirmation). Two independent extractions per figure: LLM vision with calibrated axes and a manual digitiser; reconcile disagreements > 0.05. Metrics vs the table: sd and bias of levels and adjacent log SF, inter-extractor sd, attenuation slope (regression of digitised on table deviations; Gd-dip ratio). In-corpus software part: paired comparison in the 3 FIG+TAB publications and 12 two-location cells (excluding merges) with cell-cluster bootstrap. Pre-declared gate: sd <= 0.05, |bias| <= 0.01, inter-extractor sd <= 0.04, Gd-dip ratio in [0.8, 1.2]. Phase 2: pre-declared open-access full-text search for >= 8-Ln series; yield per 100 papers of independent series, multi-condition families and clusters new to the 13. Phase 3: freeze digitised sources as a sealed confirmation set never used for development.
kill_criterion: Figure route closed if digitisation sd of adjacent log SF > 0.08 (comparable to B1's robust residual sd 0.086) or the search yields < 10 new independent clusters. FIG/TAB difference attributed to chemistry or publication (and provenance-conditional modelling dropped) if re-digitisation repeatability sd <= 0.03 and the figure-vs-table Gd-dip ratio lies in [0.8, 1.2] with a CI excluding 0.6.
expected_effect: Probably accurate enough (sd about 0.03-0.05); +20-60 sources if yield holds, raising confirmation power for a B1-sized effect to about 0.3-0.8; attenuation >= 30 % would justify a primary-data Gd amplitude near -0.10 to -0.12.
practical_value: Tells literature miners whether figure-read values are usable as reads; tells a chemist whether fresh numeric tables need a larger Gd correction than literature curves; is the only realistic route to confirming any claim, and supplies the multi-condition families the within-lab regimes need.
risks: Hallucinated coordinates if verification is skipped; selection bias in which papers have figures; digitiser settings and axis types confound; user effort for access.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-5, contrarian-7; one shared figure-vs-table calibration serves both the attenuation question and a quantitative accuracy gate for figure mining; neither digitisation attenuation nor figure-only supply had been examined.

title: E-CENS: two-sided interval scoring at measurement limits, a label-rule sensitivity that re-levels R2 without re-ranking arms
lens: data quality (censoring as a scoring rule, no data edits)
hypothesis: Part of the gap between B1 (0.452) and 0.50 is unidentifiable: pairs whose reported log D lies at or beyond a measurement limit. Scoring such pairs as intervals raises R2 for every arm by a similar amount and leaves the ranking of arms and B1 - B0 unchanged.
rationale: V1 must never be edited, and value edits without source evidence were refused. A censoring rule edits nothing; it only states what a below-limit number can mean (an SF bound, not a number).
evidence_for: Grid (B1 / B0 R2_int, censored rows per seed): point 0.452 / 0.418 / 0; floor -4.5 0.462; -4.25 0.476; -4.0 0.487 / 0.453 / 46; -3.5 0.486; (-4, 3) 0.503 / - / 77; (-4, 2.5) 0.515 / - / 177. BP within 0.001; B1 - B0 stays +0.034-0.035; every round-4 slot contrast keeps sign and size at every grid point. The only source anchor is the same group's report treating D < 1e-4 as no extraction.
evidence_against: Only F_lo = -4 has any source anchor (one group, one diluent), F_hi none; 0.503 sits on post hoc thresholds and must not be quoted as reaching 0.50; invariant rankings mean it cannot change any model decision; interval scoring can be gamed by extreme predictions on rows expected to be censored.
test_design: Register before scoring: grid F_lo {-4.5, -4.25, -4.0, -3.5} x F_hi {inf, 3.0, 2.5}; primary sensitivity cell (-4.0, 3.0) with written rationale; full curve reported. Interval construction for y = A - B from the censored end; zero loss for rows censored on the same side at both ends; denominator the mean of exact rows. Score B0, B1, FLAT, HIST_D7 and every round-5 candidate on V1 C3 k = 3 DOPT_Q, BPG deciding, BP sensitivity, cluster_cpg intervals for contrasts. Anti-gaming: point-scored dSSE on censored rows per arm. Separate estimand, never decides a finalist; a 'limit-fragile' flag for any candidate whose sign vs B1 differs between E-A and E-CENS. By-product: one-sided conformal intervals for predicted-censored pairs.
kill_criterion: Reduced to one reported line if at the primary cell B1's R2_int - R2 < 0.01, or if B1's R2_int moves by > 0.02 between adjacent F_lo grid points (threshold-fragile).
expected_effect: B1 about 0.487 (floor only) to 0.503 (floor and ceiling); unchanged B1 - B0 and rankings, so no selection effect.
practical_value: The tool can report SFs involving D < 1e-4 or D > 1e3 as bounds ('not determinable at this detection limit'); on identifiable pairs four metals give about 0.49-0.50; the remaining gap of about +0.035 is recovered by recording detection limits, not by better models.
risks: Thresholds seen on these cells; the floor anchor is borrowed from one laboratory; two-sided censoring at 2.5 is aggressive (keep the grid visible).
novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-2; applies interval scoring now on V1 as a pure scoring rule (not only inside a future V3), makes it two-sided, and shows it re-levels without re-ranking.

title: Gate floor-aware predictors on a source-stated detection limit: the clamp's sign flips within 0.5 log of its threshold
lens: data quality (decidability gate)
hypothesis: A reads-only floor-aware predictor cannot be validated on V1: its effect depends so steeply on the floor threshold F that any F chosen on V1 is fitted to the C5-BTBP cells' labels. Only a source-stated detection limit can fix F.
rationale: The floor-aware predictor is listed as runnable in software; if its outcome is decided by a free threshold, a round-5 slot would spend power on a knife-edge or invite post hoc threshold choice. A cheap diagnostic closes or gates it first.
evidence_for: Read clamp (reads below F set to F) added to B1, BPG (BP identical to 3 decimals): F = -4.5 0.464; -4.25 0.471; -4.0 0.458; -3.75 0.411; -3.5 0.317; -3.0 -0.079 (B1 0.452). Prediction clamp at -4.25: 0.470. For F <= -4 SSE changes only on C5-BTBP rows; at -3.5 those rows lose +12.1 SSE/seed. The good window is about 0.5 log wide and sits at the cells' own floor value.
evidence_against: If the closed papers state a limit near -4.3, the predictor would give a real but source-local +0.01 to +0.02; the clamp is one of several censored forms (a smoother Tobit-type interpolation was not tried).
test_design: 1. Pre-register now: no floor-aware predictor is a round-5 decision slot unless F comes from a source document (experimental sections of the candidate source papers, or a lab's stated per-metal limit); record the exploratory F-curve as already seen. 2. When F_src arrives: run both clamps at F_src on V1 C3 k = 3 DOPT_Q, BPG deciding; report C5-BTBP rows and other rows separately; robustness band F_src +/- 0.25; control: the same clamp on a label-free random 15-cell subset of non-floor cells. 3. Any Tobit-type variant pre-specified with the same band.
kill_criterion: Floor-aware predictors retired (floors kept only in scoring, M23) if at F_src the gain vs B1 < +0.005 R2, or its sign flips anywhere in F_src +/- 0.25, or the gain comes only from pub_6a0ef8528c (then it counts as a source-local data fix, not a model claim).
expected_effect: None now (the output is a gate). With a source limit near -4.25 to -4.5, a source-local +0.01 to +0.02; with a limit at or above -3.75 the predictor would be harmful.
practical_value: A generic 'clamp below-detection values' rule is dangerous unless the limit is known to about 0.25 log; laboratories should report per-metal detection limits or '< DL' rather than a number; no software effort on floor modelling before the source arrives.
risks: 'Retired' could be misread as 'floor absent' (it means undecidable without the limit); the decisive run needs the user's journal access.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-3; first measurement of the floor predictor's threshold dependence, turning it from a candidate slot into a gate on source evidence.

title: Source recovery with an unbiased audit: a label-blind random sample plus the highest-stakes documents, frozen V3 rules and verified-only scoring
lens: data quality and provenance (desk recovery, blind double entry)
hypothesis: No-location cells hold most of B1's gain over B0. Their problem is a modest rate of gross transcription errors (decade slips, wrong figure or condition), not rounding. A blind double-entry audit of a label-free random sample estimates that rate without selection bias, and recovering the few highest-stakes documents decides whether B1's Gd term is anchored in verifiable data (B1 - B0 >= +0.02 on verified rows).
rationale: Source recovery has been requested since round 3 without a protocol. Auditing only the worst-residual cells biases any V3 toward better R2 by construction; ranking by SSE share maximises information per hour but is value-informed. Combining a blind random stratum with a labelled high-stakes stratum gives both an unbiased error rate and a decisive answer on the Gd term.
evidence_for: 79 C3 cells (25 publications) have no data location: 38.9 % of rows, 57.7 % of B1's SSE, 79.1 % of its gain; top 5 documents 40.5 % SSE / 44.1 % gain, top 10 49.6 % / 52.2 %; C5-BTBP alone 23.1 % / 34.6 %. ORNL-type imports are coarse (287 of 949 records have 1 significant figure). In six DOIs with both import and curated records only 9.5 % of matched values agree within 0.005 log (median |d| 0.05-0.07) and known integer-decade slips occur. Rounding variance is only 3.9 % of B1's SSE and keeping rows with >= 2 significant figures gives 0.451 vs random 0.452, so precision is not the driver. Stakes: 0.386 -> 0.422 without the import cells, which define 9 of 13 clusters.
evidence_against: The no-location class mixes imports, C5-BTBP and a DMDPhPDA copy and is confounded with chemotype; recovery may simply confirm values; the most valuable documents are closed or large downloads (the user is needed); the six-DOI comparison has unmatched conditions; 15 sampled of 54 gives wide intervals (0/15 -> upper bound 0.18); auditors may still recognise numbers.
test_design: (a) Software now: pre-registered condition-matching rule (DOI, metal, acid, extractant concentration, solvent, complexant; 1 % tolerance) over the 6 dual-transcribed DOIs: gross-error rate (|d log D| > 0.3 or within 0.02 of an integer decade) and sd of non-gross d adjacent log SF, with exact binomial bounds. (b) Freeze V3 rules before any recovered value is read: VERIFIED (all metals within 0.05 log for tables, 0.10 for figures with two digitisations of sd <= 0.03), MISMATCHED (source values replace), below a stated limit (censored interval targets, M23), UNLOCATABLE after a fixed search protocol, MISATTRIBUTED. (c) Two strata: a seeded label-free sample of >= 15 of the 54 import-only cells, one per publication first, frozen with a digest; and the SSE-ranked top-10 documents, labelled value-informed. (d) Two auditors transcribe blind from the source; a third adjudicates; V3 replaces only adjudicated values; references refit; V1 and V3 reported side by side; error rates extrapolated only as intervals, never as edits. (e) Score B0, B1 (fold beta) and HIST_D7 under BPG/BP on V1, V3, VERIFIED-only rows and the other cells, with a control on the 150 located cells.
kill_criterion: Decisions: B1 - B0 on VERIFIED rows < +0.01 with >= 40 % of gain-carrying documents resolved -> the Gd term is reported as a prior, not a finding; >= +0.02 -> anchored, doubt closed. Import provenance stops being a quality lever if the random-sample gross-error 95 % upper bound < 5 % and sd(d adjacent log SF) < 0.03 (and part (b) is deprioritised if (a) shows 0 gross errors outside DMDPhPDA in >= 30 matched records). Fewer than 30 % of the top-10 documents locatable -> a permanent 'unverifiable' stratum reported separately.
expected_effect: Most likely the C5-BTBP light-end values turn into floor-level interval targets and the DMDPhPDA copy is corrected by one decade; B1 about 0.47-0.49 on V3 with its gain shrinking to about +0.02; for imports, frequent small (about 0.05 log) disagreements and rare gross ones.
practical_value: Tells users whether the Gd correction (about -0.09 log at Gd) rests on checkable measurements, whether imported database entries are trustworthy as reads, and certifies or discredits the clusters that carry all cross-chemotype evidence.
risks: User time and journal access; downloads need permission; value-informed selection must stay labelled; matching rules must be frozen before looking at differences.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-4, acquisition-1; a per-document SSE and gain ranking over all no-location publications, a label-blind random audit stratum that keeps V3 unbiased, frozen verified-only scoring, and the finding that precision is not the error driver.

title: Nested data-version ladder (V1 | E-CENS | V2-S | V2 | V3) with a fragility flag, plus closure of robust-loss routes
lens: data quality and evaluation robustness
hypothesis: Round-5 conclusions can be made robust to contested data without editing V1: every contrast is reported on a fixed ladder of rule-sourced data versions, and a candidate whose sign vs B1 flips on any source-evidence rung is data-fragile and cannot be a finalist. Robust (Huber/LAD) losses add nothing and should not take a slot.
rationale: Earlier moves mixed source-evidence changes (V2 moved R2 by about 0.06), value-pattern rules (V2-5 floor readings, contrary to PROTOCOL section 9; V2 without V2-5 never run) and scoring changes. Nested, pre-declared rungs separate them and answer 'is this about the data or the model?' for every contrast.
evidence_for: E-CENS re-levels without re-ranking (M23); V2-S (source-evidence quarantines only, without V2-5) never run; stakes per rung: V2-flag cells 14.4 % of SSE, complexant cells 10.2 %, import cells 33.3 %, C5-BTBP 23.1 %. Huber and LAD Gd amplitudes -0.118 / -0.112 vs least squares -0.115; all-row R2 identical (0.4564); Huber re-scoring keeps every round-4 sign (S01 -0.06 %, S02 +4.7 %, S05 +1.2 %, S06 +1.1 %, S11 +0.08 % vs SSE changes of similar size); robust beta not driven by C5-BTBP.
evidence_against: Each rung rebuilds references (B1 fold fit, DOPT_Q covariance), and round 3's V2 reused V1 caches, so rungs are not perfectly like for like; many rungs add multiplicity; if rankings are identical everywhere the ladder is reporting overhead.
test_design: 1. Freeze rung definitions with digests and rule sources: V1 (none); E-CENS (scoring rule, M23); V2-S (documented defects with source or archive evidence); V2 (V2-S + value-pattern V2-5); V3 (blind source recovery, M25). 2. On each rung refit B0, B1 (fold beta) and HIST_D7, rebuild DOPT_Q sets with that rung's training covariance, and score every round-5 candidate under BPG (BP sensitivity) with cluster_cpg intervals; reproduction checks per rung (B0 to 1e-12 where data are unchanged). 3. One table of dSSE vs B1 per rung plus provenance-class columns (M21). 4. Fragility flag: sign differs between V1 and V2-S or V3, or the cluster interval moves from excluding to including 0. 5. Decisions use E-A on V1 only; flagged candidates cannot be finalists. 6. Huber re-scoring and Huber beta as one diagnostic line.
kill_criterion: Ladder collapsed to a single sensitivity line if, for >= 5 arms (B0, B1, HIST_D7, B2 and >= 1 round-5 candidate), dSSE % vs B1 keeps its sign and differs by < 1 percentage point across all rungs. Robust-loss closure confirmed if Huber beta differs from least-squares beta by < 0.01 and no round-4 sign changes (both already hold exploratorily).
expected_effect: No E-A gain; V2-S shows how much of round 3's V2 jump came from the value-pattern rule (probably small: 4 C3 cells, 20 pairs); no current arm fragile; robust losses closed.
practical_value: Tells users and reviewers which claims depend on contested data and which survive any defensible cleaning, prevents a 'gain' that is really a data-version change, and gives recovered sources a ready slot.
risks: Pipeline differences between rung rebuilds can masquerade as data effects; V3 is valid only after a blind protocol.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-7; nested rule-sourced rungs, the never-run V2-S rung isolating the protocol deviation, a binding fragility flag, and measured closure of robust losses.

title: Ce: reliability first, a registered null for Ce modelling, and a discriminating experiment (redox state vs contamination vs chemistry)
lens: data quality (test-retest reliability) + physics and chemistry of the Ce anomaly
hypothesis: Ce's deviation from the La-Pr chord (La/Ce + Ce/Pr = 34.2 % of B1's SSE) is a one-signed, sporadic per-sample excess (partial Ce(IV) under oxidising nitrate conditions, blank or contamination, or an analytical spike) with near-zero test-retest reliability. No universal, conditional or transferred Ce term helps under source hold-out; only measuring Ce reduces this error.
rationale: The project's reliability-before-correlation rule requires a replicate check of a derived quantity before correlating it with conditions. If the Ce deviation does not reproduce between series of the same cell, H-CE's condition gate has no power and a null would be uninformative. Physics gives sharp discriminating predictions (Ce(IV) needs nitrate and oxidising conditions; contamination scales with 1/concentration; a chemical tetrad would lift Ce and Pr together).
evidence_for: Split-series ICC (cells with >= 2 source series): Ce -0.06 (6 cells, 12 series) vs Nd 0.84, Eu 0.77, Pr 0.30. ICC by extractant 0.09, by publication 0.03. Ce chord right-skewed (skew +1.65; p05 / p50 / p95 -0.19 / +0.03 / +0.43) vs Pr -1.22; convex-tetrad prediction fails (Ce +0.056 vs Pr +0.001). Within publication, Ce vs acid -0.34 -> -0.11 (p 0.24) and Ce vs level -0.31 -> -0.02; Ce vs HCl within publication +0.19, against a Ce(IV) reading. A universal Ce potential gives +0.004 in sample but 0.000 under leave-cluster-out and leave-chemotype-out, all from C5-BTBP; cross-publication Ce transfer hurts (0.421 vs 0.427); asymmetric Ce intervals no better. In one cell figure and table differ by -0.71 at Ce.
evidence_against: Tiny n (6 cells); some 'series' are hidden-condition merges, which bias ICC down; Ce reproduces somewhat within extractant x publication; the corpus has no redox or blank metadata; M28 reports a within-publication Spearman of -0.23 and a leave-cluster-out gain of +0.009 for a Ce acid term on hidden-level errors, a direct conflict that this idea and M28 must resolve together.
test_design: 1. Enlarge the replicate set without new data: bench cells with nrep >= 2, archive value-conflict groups under identical condition keys with full La-Ce-Pr triplets, round 3's 15 replicated cells; exclude merge cells. Per-metal split-series ICC(1) with cell-cluster bootstrap; signal-injection check (add a 0.15 per-cell Ce offset) to show the design can detect reproducibility. 2. Registered diagnostic null: B1 + Ce with gamma fitted per fold, BPG and BP; within-publication analysis of Ce vs acid, extractant concentration, HCl vs HNO3, level and contact time with publication-demeaned ranks and publication bootstrap; La/Ce + Ce/Pr subgroup reported in every round-5 table. 3. Data-gated paired experiments in one DGA/HNO3 system with trace Ce: HNO3 vs HCl at matched D; fresh vs aged Ce(III) stock and with vs without a mild reductant; two metal concentrations 10x apart plus process blanks. Predictions: Ce(IV) -> excess vanishes in HCl or with reductant and is independent of concentration; contamination -> excess scales as 1/concentration and appears in blanks; chemistry -> identical in all arms.
kill_criterion: Ce modelling closed (routed to measurement and widened intervals) if the upper ICC_Ce bound < 0.3. Null falsified and Ce modelling reopened (M28) if ICC_Ce has a lower bound > 0.3 on >= 15 replicate cells, or fold-fitted B1 + Ce gives >= +0.005 in >= 4/5 BPG seeds with positive SSE change in >= 3 clusters besides C5-BTBP's, or a within-publication condition correlation has |rho| >= 0.3 with a CI excluding 0. If injected-signal recovery fails, the result is 'not decidable'. Mechanisms are decided by the experimental arms.
expected_effect: No R2 change by design; saves round-5 slots on the largest error block; a likely closure of H-CE plus a mechanism answer from the experiment.
practical_value: If a process depends on La/Ce or Ce/Pr, measure Ce, because no model trained on other sources predicts it; widen Ce-pair intervals. If the excess is Ce(IV), redox control of the feed is itself a separation lever and must be reported; curators should record Ce oxidation state, reductants and blanks.
risks: A registered null can be misread as 'no Ce chemistry' (wording: not transferable at this corpus size); replicate set may stay below 15 cells; merged-condition contamination; the experiment needs a lab.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-6, physics-5; puts a replicate reliability check and a registered null before H-CE's condition gate, runs the within-publication analysis (gap G5), and adds a physically discriminating experiment.

title: B1+ as a pre-specified 2 x 2 factorial: Ce log-acid offset x damped heavy-end continuation, with a fold-starvation diagnosis
lens: statistical modelling of the residual (scalar metal-local terms, cross-fitting with one-SE selection)
hypothesis: Two one-dimensional, pre-specified terms each improve B1 under leave-one-cluster-out and are additive because they touch disjoint rows: (a) an additive offset to the hidden Ce level, linear in log10 acid and fitted with a Huber loss; (b) a damped continuation of the last read slope beyond the heaviest read. Under BPG their gain is attenuated mainly by fold starvation (the big fold trains on 51-69 cells).
rationale: Ce pairs carry 34.2 % of B1's SSE and the 12 % of rows beyond the read hull have R2 about 0. Both are metal-local with one physically motivated degree of freedom, and scalar terms are the only kind of correction that has survived cross-fitting. A factorial tests both terms and their interaction in one slot and defines an honest 'B1+' reference. It is the positive counterpart of M27's Ce null.
evidence_for: Ce hidden-level error (sd 0.239) Spearman with log acid -0.20 (685 cell-seeds) and -0.33 on the bench; within publication -0.23 (82 cells, 13 publications; per-publication median -0.31, 5 of 7 negative); slope about -0.09 to -0.10 per decade. Leave-one-cluster-out: +0.0094 (OLS) / +0.0101 (Huber); Ce pairs 0.399 -> 0.43; intercept-only control -0.001, so the gain is the slope. Edge: leave-cluster-out +0.0051 to +0.0055; half-slope +0.0047; rows disjoint from Ce rows. Read-spike shrinkage and level-dependent shrinkage toward 0 lose (-0.004 / -0.029 / -0.003).
evidence_against: Under BPG folds the Ce term gives only +0.0014 / +0.0024 with fitted slopes from -0.113 to +0.017; a within-publication fixed-effects slope variant loses (-0.007 / -0.017); acid slopes for all metals are destructive (R2 0.27 / 0.34); the La-level gate is between-publication only; M27 finds Ce correlations vanish within publication on the bench (-0.11); the edge term is <= +0.0055 everywhere; the combined effect is likely below the 0.01 margin under BPG.
test_design: Factorial {B1, +Ce, +edge, +Ce+edge} on identical rows (V1 C3, k = 3, DOPT_Q) under BPG (deciding), BP and leave-one-cluster-out (13 folds). Ce term: delta_Ce = a + b*log10(clip(acid, 0.01, 10)), Huber loss, fitted on training cells where Ce is hidden using B1's level error under each training cell's own read set; applied only when Ce is hidden. Edge term: continuation slope d*s_last beyond the heaviest read, d fitted on training folds. Each term switched on or off by inner leave-cluster-out SSE with a one-SE rule toward off; report the inner-outer gap per fold. Controls: acid values permuted within publication (Ce); end slope drawn from another training cell with the same read geometry (edge). Outcomes: pooled R2, cluster-balanced log SSE ratio with sign-flip test (M34), La/Ce + Ce/Pr and extrapolated-row R2, all per fold type (big fold vs rest) to test starvation directly.
kill_criterion: Ce term killed if < +0.003 pooled R2 under BPG and < +0.005 under leave-cluster-out, or if the within-publication acid permutation keeps >= 50 % of its gain. Edge term killed if < +0.003 on both designs. Fold-starvation explanation rejected if the Ce gain outside the big fold is not larger than inside it.
expected_effect: BPG +0.004 to +0.008 combined; leave-cluster-out +0.010 to +0.016; La/Ce + Ce/Pr subgroup +0.02 to +0.04.
practical_value: Defines the honest reference for every later contrast. If the Ce term survives: at low acidity Ce is extracted about 0.09 log per decade of acid more than the La-Pr chord implies, so La/Ce or Ce/Pr targets at low acid need a Ce measurement. The edge term stops the reference from predicting SF = 1 for heavy pairs beyond the last measured metal.
risks: Ce-acid may be confounded with publication (floor cells, specific labs); slope instability in the starved big fold; gains below the margin are still informative as a reference but not as a claim.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: statistics-6; the factorial, the single-metal restriction justified by the destructive all-metal result, the fold-starvation test, and the negative results for spike and level shrinkage; run jointly with M27, which reaches the opposite conclusion on Ce.

title: Aqueous-complexant rule: an aqueous complexing agent cancels or inverts the Gd term
lens: physics and chemistry (log D as organic minus aqueous speciation)
hypothesis: The Gd dip in log D is the Gd anomaly of the extracted complex minus that of the aqueous species. In nitrate-only media the aqueous species is the aqua/nitrato ion and a negative dip appears (B1's beta about -0.09). When an aqueous complexing agent (aminopolycarboxylate or N-donor) dominates aqueous speciation, its own Gd anomaly is subtracted and cancels or inverts the dip. So B1's Gd term is wrong in sign in these cells, and a label-free rule (Gd term off when an aqueous complexant is present; inert nitrate salts do not count) removes a systematic error.
rationale: The form is exact from mass balance (log D = log D0 - log(1 + sum beta_aq [L]^n)). It was stated as a data-contract rule but never scored. The decisive feature is a within-laboratory negative control: the same publications contain complexant cells and nitrate-salt-only cells with the same extractant and acid range.
evidence_for: Bench Gd chord: complexant + NaNO3 cells +0.088 (6 cells, none negative); NaNO3-only cells of the same publications -0.092; no complexant -0.126 (118 cells). Projected residuals show a Gd bump for complexants and a dip for NaNO3. In complexant cells B1 is worse than B0 (SSE 1.73 vs 1.35 per seed); E3 also reports negative Gd gain there. Rule 'Gd term off in the 15 complexant cells': BPG 0.4521 -> 0.4575; complexant rows 0.398 -> 0.469; placebo (15 random non-complexant cells, 300 draws) mean 0.4494, 95 % [0.4463, 0.4521], max 0.4536. Tabulated stability constants put the aminopolycarboxylate's own Gd chord near -0.09.
evidence_against: Only 15 cells from 3 publications, all sc009 in the giant cluster (Kish about 1); the rule was checked after E3 had seen negative gain (lead); the observed shift (+0.18) is about twice the tabulated prediction and a magnitude variant scored below plain switch-off; some mixed-complexant cells give dip-like signs; complexant identity is not on the bench (it comes from provenance).
test_design: (a) Freeze an aqueous-complexant list before scoring (from provenance; inert nitrate salts excluded). (b) B1-AQ = B1 with the Gd potential set to 0 in complexant cells, beta fitted per fold on non-complexant training cells; secondary B1-AQb with u_Gd = beta - c_Gd(complexant) from tabulated constants where available. (c) Score BPG (deciding) and BP pooled R2, the complexant stratum (about 131 rows per seed), Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb R2, balanced MAE. (d) Controls: placebo distribution (Gd off in 15 random non-complexant cells, 1,000 draws); NaNO3-only negative control whose chord must stay < 0 and to which the rule does not apply; per-publication sign of the complexant chord. (e) Decisive external check: paired series from the same laboratory with and without an aqueous complexant, read before any model change; prediction: the Gd chord rises with the complexant in each pair.
kill_criterion: Killed if B1-AQ does not exceed the 97.5th percentile of the placebo in >= 4/5 BPG seeds; or dropping any one of the 3 publications removes > 70 % of the gain; or, externally, in >= 2 of 3 paired series from >= 2 laboratories the Gd chord does not rise when the complexant is added.
expected_effect: +0.004 to +0.006 pooled R2 (an in-corpus lead below the margin); complexant-stratum R2 about 0.40 -> 0.47; large for Gd pairs of any future complexant-containing source; externally a sign prediction (dip -> null or bump).
practical_value: Separation schemes that add an aqueous complexing agent are where Gd/Eu and Tb/Gd cuts are often tuned; the rule warns that such agents erase the Gd anomaly, so B1 would mispredict whether Gd follows Eu or Tb. Data contract: record complexant identity and free concentration; never apply the universal Gd term blindly.
risks: One laboratory family cannot separate 'complexant' from 'this lab's protocol' (the same-lab NaNO3 control mitigates but does not eliminate this); post hoc; tabulated constants depend on medium and ionic strength (keep the magnitude variant secondary).
novelty_vs_previous: sources: physics-1; first scored version of the aqueous-speciation subtraction, with a same-laboratory negative control, a placebo-calibrated score and an external paired-series falsification design.

title: Yttrium as a 4f-free internal probe: Y's offset from the Ln radius curve as a label-free index of non-radius chemistry
lens: physics and chemistry (Y has no 4f electrons, radius near Ho) + new data acquisition
hypothesis: Y_dev = log D(Y) - PWL_R of the measured Ln evaluated at Y's radius (CN8 about 1.019 A, between Dy and Ho) measures how far a system departs from pure size selectivity. |Y_dev| correlates with the cell's |Gd dip| and roughness (partial rho >= 0.3 controlling for slope) and flags cells where B1 fails; a Y-calibrated Gd amplitude (beta0 + kappa*Y_dev) could transfer the extractant-specific dip that no structural descriptor has transferred.
rationale: The Gd dip is extractant-specific (ICC 0.69), condition-invariant within an extractant and additive (not amplitude-scaled), so what is missing is a cheap per-cell non-amplitude handle. Y is present in every heavy-REE feed, is routinely measured by ICP-MS at no extra cost, and its known extractant-dependent position along the Ln series suggests a large, chemistry-specific signal.
evidence_for: The archive has 49 Y rows from 4 DOIs, one extractant family; at the 3 conditions with bracketing Ln reads Y_dev is -0.27, -0.26 and -0.01, the same order as the Gd dip. Literature: Y's pseudo-position moves from the Ce-Pr region to Ho-Er across carboxylic-acid extractants and sits among the middle Ln for a neutral organophosphorus extractant; Y/Ho fractionation is a geochemical non-radius tracer.
evidence_against: Untestable now (3 usable conditions); Y differs from Ln in mass and possibly hydration, so Y_dev may carry a universal offset unrelated to covalency; Y's radius depends on coordination number; Y is often absent from new sources; a Y-calibrated term needs a Y read in every deployment.
test_design: Request Y in every acquisition (M05, M11, M31, M32, M33) and digitise it from open sources. Freeze the definition before any value arrives: PWL_R through the measured Ln at the CN8 radius of Y (CN9 as sensitivity); an all-Ln version (diagnostic) and a read-only version from the k = 3 DOPT_Q reads (deployable). Endpoints on >= 20 cells from >= 8 extractant units (>= 5 laboratories): partial Spearman(|Y_dev|, |Gd dip|), (|Y_dev|, cell roughness) and (|Y_dev_reads|, cell B1 MSE), each controlling for |slope|, with unit bootstrap; permutation of Y_dev across units within donor class as control. Model arms: B1-Y (Gd beta = beta0 + kappa*Y_dev, kappa fitted leave-one-laboratory-out) on Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb; B1+Y (Y as an extra read at its radius) on Dy/Ho and Ho/Er, paired per-unit sign.
kill_criterion: With >= 20 cells from >= 8 units: killed if every partial |rho| < 0.3 or every bootstrap CI includes 0, or B1-Y does not reduce Eu/Gd + Gd/Tb SSE by >= 10 % leave-one-laboratory-out, or B1+Y loses to B1 on > 50 % of units for the Ho-region pairs. Y is then recorded for Y/Ln separation use only.
expected_effect: Unknown (data-gated); a partial rho of about 0.3-0.5 if the dip is covalency-driven; any gain confined to Gd-region and Ho-region pairs.
practical_value: Y/Ho and Y/Dy are core industrial separations and B1 makes no Y prediction today; if Y_dev tracks non-radius behaviour, one extra free analyte warns a chemist that 4-metal interpolation will be unreliable for that extractant and places Y on the curve.
risks: Requested data may never arrive from enough independent labs; Y_dev may be a universal offset; the radius convention must be fixed in advance.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: physics-6, acquisition-8; an operational Y_dev estimand (all-Ln and read-only versions), first archive values, slope-controlled thresholds, a permutation control and two scored model arms.

title: In-window non-DGA Gd-triad acquisition sized from the measured between-unit spread of the Gd dip
lens: new data acquisition (non-DGA Gd-triad series) for the donor dependence of B1's only transferable effect
hypothesis: In new non-DGA laboratory x extractant units measured with Eu, Gd and Tb all inside log D [-2, 2], the mean Gd dip is <= -0.12 log, against about -0.04 for in-window DGA units and B1's universal beta of -0.094. The donor dependence of the Gd effect is then chemistry that carries over to new laboratories.
rationale: B1's gain (94 % from Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb) is learned mostly from two provenance-pending non-DGA sources, Gd-query Kish is 2.33, and every held-out donor-class test was null on about 5 non-DGA clusters. Exploratory checks show the dip is window-inflated, so new data must be in window or donor differences stay confounded with floor artefacts, and the measured between-unit spread fixes the sample size.
evidence_for: Dip out vs in window: DGA -0.109 vs -0.034; non-DGA -0.287 vs -0.146. In-window unit level: non-DGA -0.144 (29 extractant x publication units, sd 0.138) vs DGA -0.040 (26 units). Family chords DGA -0.053, amide -0.184, N-heterocyclic -0.209; phenanthroline diamides with V-shaped D-vs-Z curves minimal at Gd have been reported. Only Sm-Dy plus anchors are needed, which many papers report.
evidence_against: A family Gd scale is +0.014 in sample but -0.001 to -0.004 under LOCO, and a per-chemotype amplitude gives no gain; power vs -0.072 if the true mean is -0.144: 0.30 / 0.45 / 0.64 / about 0.73 at 6 / 10 / 16 / 20 units (95 % half-widths 0.145 / 0.099 / 0.074 at 6 / 10 / 16); within a unit the condition-to-condition sd of the dip is 0.088, so each unit needs >= 2 conditions; open-access N-donor papers cluster in a few groups.
test_design: Acquire >= 16 (target 20) new non-DGA units, each a distinct laboratory x extractant, from open access, the SAFE audit (M33) and lab series (M11). Inclusion frozen: Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy measured; Eu, Gd, Tb within [-2, 2]; >= 2 conditions averaged; detection limit stated or derivable. Statistic: dip = log D(Gd) minus the Eu-Tb chord along -r(CN8), averaged per unit. Tests: one-sample vs -0.072; Welch vs the 26 in-window C3 DGA units. Prospective check on new units at k = 3 (reads exclude Gd): B1 with universal beta vs B1 with a non-DGA beta frozen now from the C3 in-window non-DGA units through B1's own projection; paired per-unit sign as decision statistic. Count units by laboratory and stratify by group; report how many candidates the in-window rule excluded.
kill_criterion: With >= 16 units: killed if the new non-DGA mean dip has a 95 % CI including -0.072, or the frozen non-DGA beta beats the universal beta on <= 50 % of units (donor dependence is then a property of the corpus's few non-DGA sources and the universal Gd term stays). Confirmed if the CI lies below -0.10 and the class beta wins on >= 70 % of units.
expected_effect: If chemistry: mean about -0.14 and a 10-20 % reduction of Eu/Gd + Gd/Tb SSE on N-donor units (descriptive, not a pooled R2 claim). If floor or provenance: about -0.07 to -0.09.
practical_value: Gives a chemist screening N-donor or amide ligands for Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb cuts a defensible Gd correction ('for N-donors expect Gd about 0.14 log below the Eu-Tb chord') and says whether it is safe to rely on before measuring Gd.
risks: Hidden lab effects in clustered author groups; the dip-to-beta conversion must not be refitted; the in-window rule may exclude the most selective ligands.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-6; the measured window inflation of the dip, the in-window unit-level contrast, the between-unit sd and resulting sample sizes, and a prospective frozen-beta check.

title: Rigid and preorganised chemotype stress set: how many metals are needed when the series has an interior extremum
lens: new data acquisition (rigid/preorganised chemotypes) + k ladder
hypothesis: For rigid or preorganised extractants whose series have an interior extremum, B1 with 4 DOPT_Q reads falls well below its C3 level (R2 < 0.30), and reaching 0.50 needs at least 2 more measured metals than monotone chemistry, or an extremum-aware read rule.
rationale: Radius interpolation cannot represent an interior extremum it did not read, and the strongest such shapes come from chemotypes almost absent from C3 (157/229 cells DGA). A user evaluating a new rigid ligand needs a metal-count rule the corpus cannot give.
evidence_for: 14 C3 cells (about 9 % of rows) have a smoothed interior extremum >= 0.3 log beyond both ends: B1 0.316 (B0 0.300), MSE 0.064, vs 0.468 and 0.024 on 182 monotone-like cells; B1's Gd gain there only +0.016 (label-based classification, descriptive only). gen15: 27 % of well-determined cells have an interior extremum; a shape oracle is worth +0.056 but is not predictable from the 2D graph. Literature reports V-shaped curves for phenanthroline diamides. C6 ladder 0.385 / 0.431 / 0.483 / 0.524 / 0.552 at k = 2-6; per-cell placement oracle 0.632 at k = 3.
evidence_against: Several literature extrema are aqueous log K, a different estimand that must not be substituted; some of the 14 extremum cells may be floor artefacts; the learned adaptive policy gained only +0.006 at k = 3, so an extremum-aware rule may not rescue k = 3.
test_design: Acquire >= 8 full series (>= 12 Ln, values in [-3, 3]) of rigid or preorganised extractants from >= 4 laboratories (open access plus lab or SAFE series). 'Rigid' defined before any value is seen by a fixed SMARTS list of preorganised scaffolds. Freeze B0/B1 with corpus parameters; read policies DOPT_Q (primary), BISECT and ADAPT_KINK (secondary); k = 1-6 ladder on identical strict-adjacent pairs. Statistics: pooled R2 per k, first k with R2 >= 0.50, per-pair R2 for pairs bracketing the extremum, per-laboratory reporting. Control: the same ladder on >= 8 newly acquired monotone non-DGA series (from M05, M31, M33), separating 'new source' from 'shape' effects.
kill_criterion: Killed (no chemotype-specific rule needed) if B1 at k = 3 on the rigid set reaches >= 0.40 and the first k reaching 0.50 is within 1 read of the monotone control. Supported if B1 at k = 3 < 0.30 and the rigid set needs >= 2 more reads than the control.
expected_effect: About 0.3 at k = 3; a likely rule 'for preorganised N-donors measure >= 7 metals including both neighbours of the expected extremum'.
practical_value: A measured minimum metal count, and where to place the reads, for a chemist who has just made a rigid size-selective ligand, which are the ligands most likely to give unusual adjacent selectivity.
risks: Small n and family clustering; plotted values need double digitisation (M22).
novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-7; a descriptive penalty for extremum cells in C3, a frozen k ladder with a monotone new-data control, and a decision rule phrased as a metal count.

title: Label-blind SAFE + open-access novelty audit feeding a balanced, equal-weight transport check of B1
lens: new data acquisition (export audit) + transport estimand reachable at small G
hypothesis: SAFE records newer than the archive (+1,618, +9.6 %) plus open-access literature hold >= 10 new laboratory x chemotype units with >= 5-Ln series. That is enough for a frozen external check of whether B1's level and its sign over B0 transport to unseen laboratories (equal weight per unit), a different and reachable estimand compared with sealed delta-R2 confirmation.
rationale: Confirmation of a model gain is out of reach (power <= 0.10 at G = 5-10), but a transport check of B1's level at G about 10 can tell 'transports at about 0.5' from 'collapses below 0.35'. A label-blind count of the SAFE delta is the cheapest way to learn whether such a set exists before spending the user's time.
evidence_for: Equal-weight resampling of C3 units (no extra per-source noise): B1 mean 0.525 (37 publication units) and 0.50 (31 chemotype units); 95 % ranges [0.302, 0.748] / [0.364, 0.694] / [0.404, 0.642] at G = 5 / 10 / 20; P(B1 > B0) 0.80 / 0.89 / 0.95. One balanced cell per lab x chemotype gives Kish = G; Kish failure kills 26-47 % of sets at G <= 20. SAFE's schema matches the bundle.
evidence_against: Equal-weight R2 is not pooled R2 and must never be quoted as 'reaching 0.50'; the resampling is optimistic (with per-source noise power is much lower); the SAFE delta may be mostly single-Ln or non-Ln records; new papers on known chemotypes add no clusters.
test_design: (1) The user logs in and exports Ln records (Claude never logs in). (2) An audit script reads only metadata columns (record ID, DOI, data location, extractant name/SMILES, metal, conditions, authors) and asserts that the D column is never loaded; it computes DOIs absent from master_clean, conditions with >= 5 Ln and kmax >= 3, nearest-C3 Tanimoto (Morgan r = 2, 0.7) and family map, and laboratory identity from author sets, and outputs a pre-declared unit list plus verified open-access units. (3) If >= 10 units, freeze V-EXT: one condition per unit chosen from metadata or reads only (most metals in [-2, 2]), DOPT_Q reads, B0/B1/HIST_D7 with corpus parameters; score once; report equal-weight R2, pooled R2, per-unit B1 - B0 sign, conformal coverage and direction accuracy. (4) Record Y, detection limit and data location per unit (feeds M30 and M25).
kill_criterion: Fewer than 3 new units: stop pursuing SAFE and recommend lab campaigns only. 3-9 units: descriptive check only. >= 10 units with B1's equal-weight R2 upper 95 % bound < 0.40, or B1 < B0 on > 50 % of units: B1 declared non-transportable and the deployment claim restricted to corpus-like chemistry.
expected_effect: Equal-weight B1 about 0.50-0.52 with about +-0.15 at G = 10 and P(B1 > B0) about 0.9; audit yield 5-15 units (uncertain).
practical_value: The only route to telling a chemist from a laboratory outside the corpus whether 4-metal predictions and their intervals hold for their kind of data, plus a go/no-go before any values are seen.
risks: Unit identity must be decided from metadata before values are read; the condition rule must never use hidden metals; SAFE terms of use must be checked by the user.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-4; a label-blind column contract, a unit-count go/no-go ladder and a reframing toward a transport estimand reachable at G about 10, with new resampling numbers.

title: Few-cluster-valid paired tests: cluster sign-flip randomisation on (log) SSE ratios and an Ibragimov-Muller t-test, calibrated by a heavy-tailed hierarchical simulator
lens: evaluation and inference design (few large heterogeneous clusters)
hypothesis: With 13 clusters (Kish 2.24), a cluster sign-flip randomisation test (pooled dSSE or the mean per-cluster log SSE ratio) and an IM t-test across per-cluster relative SSE keep size <= 0.05-0.075 under calibrated nulls and have clearly more power than the sealed percentile/BCa/jackknife triple, reaching >= 0.6 power at 6-8 new sources for a B1-sized consistent effect.
rationale: The sealed rule is both anti-conservative (5-8 % vs nominal 2.5 % under the boundary null) and powerless (B1 - B0 jackknife interval includes 0). Tests built for few large clusters count the giant cluster once; the log SSE ratio is antisymmetric under arm swap, which is the symmetry the sign-flip test needs, and its smallest p is 2^-G without asymptotics in G.
evidence_for: B1 - B0: 11 of 12 non-tied clusters better; pooled sign-flip p 0.0032 (exact); equal-weight sign-flip p 0.014; mean log SSE ratio +0.160, sign-flip p 0.007 (BPG and BP); IM t 2.60, p 0.012; publication level 31/38, p 0.0001. Every round-4 slot stays null (p >= 0.12); S02's pooled loss is a big-fold effect (+0.017 on the balanced metric). Smallest attainable p 0.031 at G = 5, 0.016 at G = 6.
evidence_against: B1 - B0 on development data checks sensitivity, not confirmation; exactness needs independent clusters and sign symmetry; pooled sign-flip inherits giant-cluster dominance (one cluster holds 83-86 % of |dSSE| for S02, S06); HBK@ML - B0 rejects under equal weighting (p 0.017) but not pooled (0.46), which is either a real small-cluster gain or a false positive; tiny clusters make relative SSE heavy-tailed; the round-4 generator was miscalibrated (S05 and S11 gained +0.02 in null worlds).
test_design: (1) One generator built from B1's real OOF residuals: per-cell offset (36 % of pointwise energy), AR(1) drift along hidden runs (rho 0.69), metal-specific Student-t spikes, publication x pair effects, same-extractant cross-publication correlation 0.10-0.14, cluster heterogeneity tau 0.065. Calibrate to kurtosis 18.2, top 1 % / 5 % SSE shares 31 % / 59 %, lag-1 / lag-2 pair correlations -0.522 / +0.091, the K curve of publication offsets, per-cluster SSE shares and the real per-cluster dSSE spread of near-null contrasts; accept only if every target lies in its bootstrap 90 % band. (2) Worlds: exchangeable null; heterogeneous zero-mean null (small-cluster gains, equal giant-cluster loss); SSE-preserving boundary null; effects delta = 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.034, homogeneous and heterogeneous; >= 200 replicates; development geometry and new-source sets G = 5, 8, 10, 13, 20, 40. (3) Tests: sealed rule (control), pooled and equal-weight cluster sign-flip, sign-flip on mean log SSE ratio and a studentised version, publication sign-flip, IM-t on relative SSE and on log ratio, jackknife-t with Kish df, CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey df, wild cluster restricted bootstrap with Webb weights. (4) Before any round-5 contrast is scored, declare one test per estimand (pooled -> sign-flip; equal-weight -> IM-t) with balanced MAE as a non-inferiority guard.
kill_criterion: A test is dropped if its size exceeds 0.075 at nominal 0.05 in any calibrated null world (heterogeneous null included), or its power at delta = 0.034, G = 20 is not >= the sealed rule's + 0.10. If the sign-flip test has power < 0.3 at G = 8 for a B1-sized effect, keep POWER.md's 40-80-source conclusion and treat round-5 model contrasts as diagnostics.
expected_effect: Nominal size and about 2-3x the sealed rule's power for consistent effects; power 0.5-0.8 at G = 6-8 for a B1-sized effect; < 0.2 for +0.01 effects; no round-4 verdict changes.
practical_value: 'Did the Gd correction help in most independent sources?' becomes testable: development evidence now, confirmation with about 6-20 new sources instead of 40-80.
risks: Equal weighting answers 'the average source', not 'the average row', and must never replace pooled R2; simulator misspecification; clusters not fully independent (copy groups, shared labs); the choice must be sealed before new data.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-1, statistics-4; first few-cluster-valid tests computed on this corpus, a residual-calibrated generator (gap G7), and a balanced re-scoring of round-4 slots (gap G4).

title: One currency for decisions: pooled and equal-weight relative pair-SSE vs B1 as co-primary, balanced-MAE guard, BPG deciding, mandatory per-cluster and fold-type tables, replayed on all stored arms
lens: evaluation design (decision metric and margins)
hypothesis: A decision rule written entirely in relative pair-SSE vs B1 (pooled reduction >= 2 %; equal-weight cluster mean > 0 by IM-t; balanced MAE change >= -0.001) passes the one known positive (B1 vs B0), rejects every round-4 loser, and has about 1.5x the signal-to-noise of delta R2 with a 0.005 balanced-MAE margin. Where the two weightings disagree, the result is a lead, not a claim.
rationale: The current margins are in different currencies (0.005 balanced MAE is about +0.034-0.053 R2; block A's MAE leg was unreachable even as an oracle), pooled R2 weights the giant cluster at 0.65, and the deciding fold trains on 51-69 cells. Relative SSE vs B1 is one currency (2 % about +0.011 R2 about 0.0015 balanced MAE) with a pooled and an equal-cluster form.
evidence_for: B1 - B0 under each statistic (cluster-jackknife t): delta R2 +0.034 (1.73); relative SSE pooled +5.9 % (1.99); sqrt(n)-weighted +9.3 % (2.55); equal-weight +12.4 % (2.60); log ratio +15.1 % (2.89). Replay: B1 - B0 passes all three legs (5.9 %, IM p 0.012, +0.005 MAE); every other arm fails the pooled leg (S01 -0.02 %, S02 -4.4 %, S05 -1.1 %, S06 -1.0 %, S11 -0.1 %, B2 -4.0 %, HIST_D7 -0.2 %). In the non-big folds no round-4 slot reaches 2 % either, so the big fold hid no gain.
evidence_against: The weighting changes conclusions: S02 is -4.4 % pooled but +1.0-1.5 % equal-weight (9 of 13 clusters better, IM p 0.24); HBK@ML - B0 is +0.13 % pooled but +7 % equal-weight (IM p 0.017), contradicting the FIRM 'learned curve models <= PWL' under that weighting, though it fails Holm over about 15 contrasts; equal weighting gives 1-2-cell clusters the voice of the 162-cell cluster.
test_design: 1. Seal before any round-5 score: E-A pooled R2 (continuity); co-primary relative pair-SSE vs B1, pooled (margin >= 2 %) and equal-weight cluster mean (IM-t, one-sided 0.05; test choice from M34); guard balanced MAE change >= -0.001; BPG decides and BP is a labelled sensitivity; mandatory per-cluster (13 rows), per-fold-type and six-design diagnostic tables. 2. Retrospective replay (minutes) with Holm on stored OOF predictions of REF, S01, S02, S05, S06, S11, R3-R02, R3-R14, LINE, RIDGE2, HBK@ML, G14@ZERO, B2, HIST_D7: must pass B1 - B0 and reject every round-4 slot. 3. Disagreement rule: one weighting negative and the other significant -> a weighting-dependent lead registered as an E-B contrast; first candidate HBK@ML base plus a fold-fitted Gd amplitude vs B1, reported per cluster.
kill_criterion: Co-primary abandoned if the replay fails B1 - B0 or passes any round-4 slot, or if in calibrated synthetic worlds (M34) the equal-weight signal-to-noise for a B1-like effect is not >= 1.3x that of delta R2. The HBK@ML lead is dropped if its E-B contrast vs B1 is <= 0 or has IM p > 0.05.
expected_effect: The 0.452 reference is unchanged; margin legs become consistent; about 1.5x signal-to-noise for consistent effects; a written rule for disagreements.
practical_value: One number with two readings: how much a method helps the average pair, and whether it helps the average independent laboratory; if the HBK@ML flag is real, learned curve models help small unusual sources while tying on the DGA-dominated pool.
risks: The equal-weight leg invites cherry-picking unless sealed first; tiny clusters flip signs by noise; changing currency breaks comparability unless E-A stays reported.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-2; the signal-to-noise table, the replay against every stored arm, the S02 and HBK@ML weighting flips, and the check that per-fold-type reporting would not have changed any round-4 verdict.

title: Publication vs cluster confirmation units: calibrated simulation using the measured within-cluster publication ICC
lens: evaluation and inference design (H-UNIT)
hypothesis: A publication-level confirmation test (sign test or IM-t over publications, optionally chemotype-stratified) keeps size <= 0.075 only when publication gains are not too strongly shared within clusters; at the measured ICC this holds only with chemotype stratification or independent-lab layouts. If valid, 10-20 new publications can confirm a B1-like consistent gain; if not, confirmation needs >= 40 cluster-level sources.
rationale: Publication Kish 18.8 vs cluster Kish 2.24 is the difference between a feasible and an infeasible confirmation, and validity depends on how strongly gains are shared across publications of the same chemistry, which can be measured on the development corpus and carried into a simulation.
evidence_for: ICC of per-publication relative gain within clusters (30 publications in 4 multi-publication clusters): B1 - B0 0.11; S02 - B1 0.29; S05 - B1 0.29; HIST_D7 - B1 0.33. Probit toy on the real layout: publication sign test size 0.027 under independence, 0.064 / 0.104 / 0.137 / 0.198 at latent rho 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5. B1 - B0's 31/38 stays significant even at rho 0.5 (0.019). Cross-publication same-extractant residual correlation 0.10-0.14.
evidence_against: The toy is a probit on win indicators, not the round-5 generator; ICCs come from 4 clusters, one with 19 publications; new sources may arrive as 2-3 publications of one chemotype (the worst case); literature supply is 3-5 sources.
test_design: Use the M34 generator with publication-within-cluster ICC in {0.1, 0.2, 0.33}, cross-publication same-extractant correlation 0.10-0.14 and the light-end/Ce tail. New-source batches of G = 5, 10, 20, 40 publications in three layouts: independent labs; 2-3 publications per chemotype; the development layout. >= 200 replicates per world x layout x G. Worlds: exchangeable null, heterogeneous zero-mean null, B1-like effects at delta 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.034. Tests: publication sign test, publication IM-t, chemotype-stratified publication permutation, cluster sign-flip, cluster IM-t, sealed rule. Report size, power and the G giving 80 % power per test and layout.
kill_criterion: Publication units rejected for layouts with shared chemotypes if their size exceeds 0.075 at ICC >= 0.1, and entirely if size exceeds 0.075 even with independent labs; the planning number then stays at >= 40 cluster-level sources and model confirmation from literature batches is no longer planned.
expected_effect: Publication units valid only with chemotype stratification or independent-lab layouts; about 15-20 publications for 80 % power on a B1-like consistent effect; effects <= 0.01 unconfirmable.
practical_value: Decides whether a modest literature-plus-collaborator campaign can ever confirm a claim, and tells the data request to ask for many independent laboratories rather than more chemistry from the same ones.
risks: ICC from only 4 clusters; publication units valid here may be anti-conservative for chemistries outside the corpus; never relabel development results as confirmed.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-4; the measured within-cluster publication ICC of nuisance contrasts and a size-inflation curve on the real layout showing a naive publication unit is anti-conservative.

title: Sequential confirmation ledger valid at any stopping point: an e-process on 'beats B1 on a new independent source', with a magnitude guard
lens: evaluation and inference design (anytime-valid sequential testing)
hypothesis: Freezing one finalist and running an e-process on per-source win indicators (or bounded per-source relative SSE) keeps type-I error <= 0.05 under optional stopping and across rounds, and reaches 70-90 % power for a B1-like consistent gain within 20-30 new sources, which realistic supply can reach over several rounds; the fixed-G sealed rule never can.
rationale: Supply arrives in trickles (0-2 repository and 3-5 literature sources per round), while the sealed rule needs one batch of 40-80 and spends alpha at every look. Test martingales allow adding sources one at a time and stopping early for success or futility, and the per-source estimand is what a user cares about.
evidence_for: Fixed-bet e-process (lambda 0.6, reject at E >= 20), 20,000 runs: size 0.007-0.035 at pi = 0.5 for G = 8-40. Power at pi = 0.8: 0.21 / 0.40 / 0.54 / 0.73 / 0.91 at G = 8 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 30, vs fixed sign test 0.38 (G 10) / 0.80 (G 20) and sealed rule 0.14 at G = 20; median stop 7-13 sources. Development win rates: B1 - B0 31/38 publications (0.82), 11/12 clusters; near-null contrasts 13-22 of 37-39.
evidence_against: Candidates with delta <= 0.01 win on about 45-60 % of sources, where every design is powerless; win indicators discard magnitude (hence the guard); new sources may differ from C3, so the development pi is not the confirmation pi.
test_design: 1. Register estimand pi = P(candidate SSE < B1 SSE on a new independent source's strict-adjacent queries at k = 3, DOPT_Q), with guards: running pooled relative SSE >= 0 and a betting e-process on per-source relative SSE bounded to [-1, 1]. 2. Freeze one finalist per claim and record its code hash. 3. Score each arriving source once on arrival, append with provenance and date; merge same-cluster sources into one unit (rule from M36). 4. Stop for success at E >= 20; for futility when the 95 % confidence-sequence upper bound on pi < 0.65; never reset. 5. Before use, simulate with the M36 generator under an arrival schedule of 3-7 sources per round for pi in {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9} and the heterogeneous zero-mean null (>= 200 replicates).
kill_criterion: Abandoned if, in the calibrated generator, a B1-like effect (delta 0.034, tau 0.065) has pi <= 0.65, or the e-process size exceeds 0.05 in any null world. The programme then states that no model claim is confirmable at realistic supply and moves confirmation effort to measurement (M11, M25).
expected_effect: B1-like effects confirmed after roughly 10-25 new independent sources over 3-5 rounds; effects <= 0.01 stopped for futility within about 15 sources.
practical_value: A cumulative, honest answer ('the Gd correction helped on 9 of 10 new laboratories') with a stopping rule, and a stated probability that the method helps on a chemist's own new system.
risks: Any re-tuning of the finalist voids the e-process; sources must be scored blind to inclusion decisions; win-only estimands reward tiny gains without the guard; the confirmation itself is data-gated.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-6; first per-source design valid at any stopping point, with computed size and power and development win rates showing which claims could ever pass.

title: Pre-slot decidability gate (class ceiling, development MDE, P(level >= target) band, training-size check), replayed on rounds 3-4
lens: evaluation design (prospective power and decidability)
hypothesis: Four checks that do not look at a slot's outcome (cross-fitted ceiling of the hypothesis class >= the margin; development MDE <= the plausible effect; for level claims, cluster probability P(level >= 0.50) outside [0.2, 0.8]; for learned models, ability to beat B1 with about 60 training cells in the non-giant folds) would have retired all five round-4 losers and a pass/fail 'k = 4 reaches 0.50' slot, while passing B1 - B0.
rationale: Round 4 spent 5 slots on contrasts of -0.024 to -0.0001 whose class ceilings were below the margin even as oracles; one fold decides and trains on 51-69 cells; the 0.50 aspiration sits inside a cluster interval of about +-0.05, so 'reaches 0.50' is a coin flip at current estimates.
evidence_for: Ceilings: donor x pair-type cross-fit -0.041 and oracle +0.0004 balanced MAE, so S01 and S02 retire. MDE: S05 - B1 0.011 and S11 - B1 0.003 vs plausible effects <= 0.005 / <= 0.002 (diagnostics only); B1 - B0 passes (equal-weight IM t 2.6). Level band (2,000 cluster draws): B1 all rows 0.452 [0.394, 0.508], P(>= 0.50) 0.03; B1 inside the window 0.540 [0.448, 0.576], P 0.80; the k = 4 estimate 0.495-0.503 sits at P about 0.5 by construction. The giant cluster holds 162 of 229 cells, so cluster-isolating designs train it on <= 67 cells.
evidence_against: A noisy ceiling estimate can kill a true effect; the MDE needs a pilot estimate of how far the candidate departs from B1; the bootstrap under-covers at Kish 2.24 so P(>= 0.50) is approximate; a learned model may need > 60 cells and still be useful in other regimes.
test_design: Before each slot compute: (a) the cross-fitted ceiling of the hypothesis class under BPG (leave-own-chemotype or leave-own-cluster shift of B1's residual on the class's features); (b) the development MDE at 80 % for the registered test (M34/M35) from a one-seed pilot's per-cluster dSSE spread; (c) for level claims, the cluster-bootstrap P(level >= target); (d) for learned models, non-giant-fold dSSE when trained on 5 random 60-cell subsets vs the full ~209 cells. Run as a decision slot only if ceiling >= 2 % SSE, MDE <= plausible effect, P outside [0.2, 0.8], and no > 60-cell requirement; otherwise run as a labelled diagnostic. Level claims failing the band report the paired increment (k = 4 minus k = 3, about +0.044-0.052) and the k at which P >= 0.8. Freeze thresholds, then replay on S01, S02, S05, S06, S11, B2, R02, R14/B1 and the Gd term.
kill_criterion: Gate dropped as miscalibrated if the replay retires B1 - B0 or the Gd term, or lets >= 2 of the 5 round-4 losers through as decision slots. Check (d) alone dropped if 60-cell and full training show no difference for S02 and S05.
expected_effect: Fewer, better-powered decision slots in round 5; the 0.50 aspiration reported as P(level >= 0.50) with an interval rather than a pass/fail point.
practical_value: Stops spending compute and analyst degrees of freedom on questions the corpus cannot answer; statements such as 'five measured metals reach 0.50' come with the probability that they hold for new sources.
risks: Tuning the gate's thresholds after the replay adds another forking path; freeze them first.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-7; one pre-slot gate combining class ceiling, MDE, a level band and a training-size check, with a replay it must pass on B1 - B0.

title: Nested re-estimation of the five post hoc leads before registration (window, K, edge damping, half-slope, max-min 5th read)
lens: evaluation design (selection optimism)
hypothesis: Re-running each analyst's selection step inside the outer folds (choose on the other folds' OOF rows, apply to the held-out fold) exposes a measurable optimism for each lead. Leads that still meet their decision thresholds after nesting can be registered; the rest are retired or kept as diagnostics.
rationale: The evidence base lists five post hoc choices as leads, not results, and round 4 showed inner selection was optimistic (outer SSE worse in 12 of 14 fold-fits that chose a correction). A nested replay prices the selection step on the same data without new data.
evidence_for: Window: nested half-width choice (inside R2 at coverage >= 0.70) gives 0.527 at 75.3 % vs 0.540 post hoc; h = 2 chosen in 21 of 25 folds; the curve is monotone (h 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 / 2.5 / 3.0: coverage 45.5 / 60 / 75 / 85 / 93 %, inside R2 0.571 / 0.557 / 0.540 / 0.501 / 0.495), so [-2, 2] is not a peak. Matched-coverage controls: random abstention stratified by pair type x cluster 0.477 [0.466, 0.488] (max 0.493); dropping La/Ce, Ce/Pr, Pr/Nd 0.466 at 78 %; dropping out-of-hull rows 0.472 at 88 %. Publication x pair offsets: best fixed K = 5 (0.533); nested choice 0.526 (K = 5 in 16 of 25 folds).
evidence_against: Nesting on the same 229 cells removes selection optimism within the grid but not the choice of grid, estimator family or idea; the window abstains on 81 % of the BTBP cluster's rows, so part of its gain is provenance; levels near 0.53 carry a cluster interval of about +-0.05 (M38).
test_design: 1. Freeze the grids the analysts actually considered: window (the 4 published windows plus a 6-point half-width grid); K in {0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50}; edge damping d in {0, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.75, 1} (covers the half-slope rule); 5th-read policy in {random, max-min, DOPT_Q-nested, Gd-first, BISECT}. 2. Fix the selection criterion in advance (SSE, or inside R2 at coverage >= 0.70). 3. Per seed and outer fold select on the other folds' OOF rows and apply to the held-out fold; pool folds, average seeds. 4. Report nested value, optimism (post hoc minus nested), share of folds choosing the post hoc value, cluster intervals. 5. Controls: stratified random abstention and drop-light-pairs (window); noise-matched linear tail (edge); random legal read on identical queries (5th read). 6. Register the window as the full coverage-R2 curve with operating points at coverage 0.75 and 0.90 fixed now (shared with M09).
kill_criterion: A lead is retired if its nested value misses its threshold (window: inside R2 < 0.50 at coverage >= 0.70, or not above the stratified control by >= 0.03; publication offsets: < B1 + 0.02; edge continuation: < +0.003; max-min 5th read: < DOPT_Q-nested + 0.005), or if its post hoc value is chosen in fewer than 50 % of folds.
expected_effect: Window survives (about 0.527 at 75 %, about +0.05 over the stratified control); publication offsets survive (0.526); edge rules and max-min shrink to about +0.002-0.004 and +-0.005 and are retired or kept as diagnostics.
practical_value: Honest numbers before they are advertised ('when both predicted log D lie in [-2, 2], expect R2 about 0.53 on three quarters of pairs; outside about 0.30'), and fewer round-5 slots spent on leads that only look good after selection.
risks: A nested value is a debiased lead, not a result; the window's operating points must be fixed now and labelled as fixed after this analysis.
novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-3; nested values for two of the five leads, the monotone curve showing [-2, 2] is not a peak, and stratified and cheapest-alternative controls.
